explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF p. 238

explanations.explanation_text: The spinal cord gives rise to 31 pairs of spinal nerves (8 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral, 1 coccygeal), not 29.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF pp. 232, 238

explanations.explanation_text: During wound healing and fibrous scar maturation, early delicate type III collagen is systematically turned over and replaced by dense, densely packed, parallel bundles of Type I collagen, which impart high tensile resistance but lack elasticity, thereby reducing tissue pliability.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 4 (PDF p. 64) & printed p. 9 (PDF p. 69)

explanations.explanation_text: During wound healing and fibrous scar maturation, early delicate type III collagen is systematically turned over and replaced by dense, densely packed, parallel bundles of Type I collagen, which impart high tensile resistance but lack elasticity, thereby reducing tissue pliability.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 9 (PDF p. 69)

explanations.explanation_text: Reticular fibers (type III collagen) form delicate, flexible supportive meshes in glandular organs and bone marrow, not dense mature scar tissue.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 9 (PDF p. 69)

explanations.explanation_text: Secondary polycythemia is characterized by ELEVATED erythropoietin levels; low serum erythropoietin is the classic hallmark of primary polycythemia vera.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (3) 2027 pathology.pdf, printed p. 18 (PDF p. 19)

explanations.explanation_text: Activating mutations in the JAK2 gene (JAK2 V617F) are the molecular driver of primary Polycythemia Vera, not secondary polycythemia.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (3) 2027 pathology.pdf, printed p. 18 (PDF p. 19)

explanations.explanation_text: Secondary polycythemia is defined by an absolute increase in red cell mass.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (3) 2027 pathology.pdf, printed p. 18 (PDF p. 19)

explanations.explanation_text: Vancomycin is a glycopeptide antibiotic that binds D-Ala-D-Ala and is highly effective and widely used for severe infections caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA).
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 36 (PDF p. 39)

explanations.explanation_text: Vancomycin inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding to the D-Ala-D-Ala terminus of peptidoglycan, not by inhibiting ribosomal subunits.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 36 (PDF p. 39)

explanations.explanation_text: Vancomycin is not absorbed orally; it must be administered by slow IV infusion for systemic infections.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 36 (PDF p. 39)

explanations.explanation_text: Vancomycin belongs to the glycopeptide class, not the macrolide class.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 36 (PDF p. 39)

explanations.explanation_text: Erythromycin (a macrolide) reversibly binds to the 50S bacterial ribosomal subunit and blocks the translocation step of protein synthesis.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed pp. 37, 42 (PDF pp. 40, 45)

explanations.explanation_text: Tetracycline binds to the 30S ribosomal subunit, preventing aminoacyl-tRNA access.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed pp. 37, 38 (PDF pp. 40, 41)

explanations.explanation_text: Gentamicin is an aminoglycoside that binds specifically to sites on the 30S ribosomal subunit.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed pp. 37, 40 (PDF pp. 40, 43)

explanations.explanation_text: Penicillin G inhibits cell wall transpeptidase (PBPs); it has no effect on ribosomes.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 30 (PDF p. 33)

explanations.explanation_text: Chloramphenicol accumulates in neonates due to low hepatic UDP-glucuronyltransferase activity and immature renal excretion, inhibiting mitochondrial ribosomes and causing hypothermia, cyanosis, cardiovascular collapse, and gray skin discoloration (gray baby syndrome).
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 45 (PDF p. 48)

explanations.explanation_text: Amoxicillin is safe in neonates and does not cause mitochondrial ribosome toxicity or gray baby syndrome.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 32 (PDF p. 35)

explanations.explanation_text: Ciprofloxacin causes arthropathy and cartilage damage in pediatric patients, not gray baby syndrome.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 51 (PDF p. 54)

explanations.explanation_text: Rifampin causes reddish-orange discoloration of bodily fluids and hepatotoxicity, not gray baby syndrome.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 28 (PDF p. 31)

explanations.explanation_text: Penicillins do NOT produce a disulfiram-like reaction.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed pp. 33, 35 (PDF pp. 36, 38)

explanations.explanation_text: Hypersensitivity reactions are the most frequent adverse effects of penicillins, occurring in about 5% of patients.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 33 (PDF p. 36)

explanations.explanation_text: Severe IgE-mediated anaphylactic shock is a recognized life-threatening risk of penicillin administration.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 33 (PDF p. 36)

explanations.explanation_text: Respiratory pseudostratified epithelium is characteristically richly populated with mucus-secreting goblet cells.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 4 (PDF p. 44)

explanations.explanation_text: Elastic fibers confer elastic recoil and flexibility; they are poorly synthesized and markedly deficient in mature fibrotic scar tissue, which explains why scars remain stiff and non-distensible.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 9 (PDF p. 69)

explanations.explanation_text: Cholesterol molecules are intercalated between the hydrophobic fatty acid tails of the phospholipid bilayer, where they act as a bidirectional fluidity buffer: preventing membrane crystallization/rigidity at low temperatures and restricting excessive phospholipid movement and leakiness at high temperatures.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 4 (PDF p. 12)

explanations.explanation_text: Integral transmembrane proteins serve as channels, transporters, pumps, and receptors, but do not act as the primary physicochemical regulator of lipid bilayer fluidity.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 4 (PDF p. 12)

explanations.explanation_text: The glycocalyx is involved in cell recognition, immune identity, and protective cushion on the outer leaflet, not internal bilayer fluidity.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 4 (PDF p. 12)

explanations.explanation_text: Peripheral membrane proteins associate transiently with membrane surfaces to provide cytoskeletal anchorage or signal transduction, without modulating lipid fluidity.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 4 (PDF p. 12)

explanations.explanation_text: Immune-mediated Coombs-positive hemolytic anemia can be triggered by penicillins binding to red blood cell membranes.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 33 (PDF p. 36)

explanations.explanation_text: Benzathine penicillin G is a long-acting depot formulation administered intramuscularly once monthly for secondary prophylaxis against Streptococcus pyogenes reinfection in patients with rheumatic fever.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed pp. 32, 33 (PDF pp. 35, 36)

explanations.explanation_text: The femur is classified as a long bone, possessing a tubular shaft and expanded epiphyses, not an air-filled bone.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF pp. 121, 122, 145

explanations.explanation_text: The scapula is classified as a flat bone, consisting of thin compact plates enclosing cancellous bone.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF pp. 121, 123, 138

explanations.explanation_text: Vertebrae are classified as irregular bones due to their complex, multi-angled morphology.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF pp. 121, 124, 132

explanations.explanation_text: The maxilla is a classic pneumatic bone; it encloses the largest of the paranasal sinuses (the maxillary air sinus), which lightens facial skull weight and provides vocal resonance.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF pp. 121, 123, 213

explanations.explanation_text: Under chronic chemical irritation and toxic stress from cigarette smoke, the delicate pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium of the bronchi undergoes squamous metaplasia, transforming reversibly into tough, protective non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium; although more resistant to toxins, this transformed epithelium lacks cilia and goblet cells, abolishing the mucociliary escalator.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 4 (PDF p. 44) & printed p. 6 (PDF p. 46)

explanations.explanation_text: An increase in individual cell size is defined as hypertrophy, whereas hyperplasia is an increase in cell number; neither defines the adaptive phenotypic switch of respiratory epithelium.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 1 (PDF p. 41)

explanations.explanation_text: In chronic smokers, bronchial submucosal mucous glands undergo dramatic hyperplasia and hypertrophy to produce excess mucus, rather than atrophying.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 4 (PDF p. 44)

explanations.explanation_text: Under chronic chemical irritation and toxic stress from cigarette smoke, the delicate pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium of the bronchi undergoes squamous metaplasia, transforming reversibly into tough, protective non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium; although more resistant to toxins, this transformed epithelium lacks cilia and goblet cells, abolishing the mucociliary escalator.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 4 (PDF p. 44) & printed p. 5 (PDF p. 45)

explanations.explanation_text: Euchromatin represents uncoiled, transcriptionally active chromatin in healthy, metabolically active cells, the exact opposite of stressed, transcriptionally silent condensed chromatin.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 16 (PDF p. 24)

explanations.explanation_text: Severe cellular stress or early apoptotic injury leads to inactivation of RNA polymerases, histone deacetylation, and supercoiling of chromatin threads, causing heterochromatin to aggregate and condense along the inner periphery of the nuclear envelope (peripheral heterochromatin condensation / nuclear pyknosis), manifesting with deep basophilia and transcriptional shutdown.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 16 (PDF p. 24) & printed p. 4 (PDF p. 30)

explanations.explanation_text: Duplication of the nuclear membrane is not a cellular stress response.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 16 (PDF p. 24)

explanations.explanation_text: Tissue macrophages (histiocytes) develop from circulating blood monocytes that leave the bloodstream by diapedesis to differentiate in connective tissues into active phagocytes.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 3 (PDF p. 63) & printed p. 5 (PDF p. 65)

explanations.explanation_text: Fibroblasts are derived from local undifferentiated mesenchymal cells (UMCs) within embryonic mesenchyme, not from hematopoietic monocytes.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 3 (PDF p. 63) & printed p. 4 (PDF p. 64)

explanations.explanation_text: Adipocytes differentiate from undifferentiated mesenchymal cells (lipoblasts), specializing in neutral fat storage.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 3 (PDF p. 63) & printed p. 4 (PDF p. 64)

explanations.explanation_text: B lymphocytes develop from common lymphoid progenitor cells in the bone marrow and give rise to antibody-secreting plasma cells, possessing a completely separate lineage from the myeloid monocyte lineage.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 3 (PDF p. 63) & printed p. 6 (PDF p. 66)

explanations.explanation_text: Actin microfilaments form the internal core skeleton of microvilli and stereocilia, as well as contractile stress fibers, not motile cilia or flagella.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 14 (PDF p. 22) & printed p. 5 (PDF p. 57)

explanations.explanation_text: Intermediate filaments (such as cytokeratins, vimentin, neurofilaments) provide mechanical strength against tensile stress, lacking motor-driven motility.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 14–15 (PDF pp. 22–23)

explanations.explanation_text: The brain (and the entire central nervous system) completely lacks true lymphatic capillaries; tissue clearance is carried out via CSF drainage and glymphatic flow.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF p. 245

explanations.explanation_text: The stomach contains mucosal and submucosal lymphatic vessels draining to regional celiac lymph nodes.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF p. 245

explanations.explanation_text: The breast has an extensive lymphatic network that drains predominantly to axillary lymph nodes.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF p. 245

explanations.explanation_text: The superior radio-ulnar joint is a uniaxial pivot joint where the radial head rotates within the annular ligament and radial notch of the ulna around a longitudinal axis, mediating forearm supination and pronation.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF pp. 157, 159

explanations.explanation_text: Deep fascia is characteristically absent in the face (with the exception of the parotid fascia and bucopharyngeal fascia covering deep structures) to permit unrestricted mobility of the muscles of facial expression during speech and emotional gesturing.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF p. 109

explanations.explanation_text: The lower limbs are tightly encased by dense, inelastic deep fascia (fascia lata in the thigh and crural fascia in the leg) that forms tough intermuscular septa and facilitates the musculovenous calf pump.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF pp. 109, 207

explanations.explanation_text: The neck possesses a complex, multi-layered deep cervical fascia (investing layer, pretracheal layer, and prevertebral layer) that supports visceral and neurovascular structures.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF p. 109

explanations.explanation_text: The thorax is invested by well-developed deep fascia (pectoral fascia, clavipectoral fascia, and endothoracic fascia) covering the thoracic musculature.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF p. 109

explanations.explanation_text: The cytoskeleton is an intricate intracellular structural network composed entirely of protein filaments and polymers, subdivided into microtubules (tubulin polymers, 24 nm), microfilaments (actin filaments, 5–7 nm), and intermediate filaments (8–10 nm) linked together by accessory bridging proteins to establish cellular shape and enable motility. Incorrect: Nucleoproteins are complexes of nucleic acids (DNA or RNA) with proteins, such as chromatin and ribosomes, whereas the cytoskeleton is composed strictly of structural protein polymers without nucleic acid components.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 12 (PDF p. 20)

explanations.explanation_text: Vancomycin is reserved for severe MRSA, enterococcal endocarditis, or penicillin-allergic surgical prophylaxis, not standard long-term rheumatic fever prophylaxis.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 36 (PDF p. 39)

explanations.explanation_text: Lacunae are the isolated matrix cavities where osteocyte cell bodies reside; they are enclosed spaces that do not themselves form the connecting communicating channels.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 4 (PDF p. 84)

explanations.explanation_text: Osteocytes communicate and exchange nutrients, metabolites, and regulatory signals with one another and with blood vessels by extending slender dendritic cytoplasmic processes through microscopic tubular channels called canaliculi, where adjacent processes form functional gap junctions.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 4 (PDF p. 84) & printed p. 8 (PDF p. 88)

explanations.explanation_text: Volkmann's canals are macroscopic transverse vascular channels carrying vessels from the periosteum into compact bone.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 5 (PDF p. 85)

explanations.explanation_text: Haversian canals are central longitudinal neurovascular conduits at the center of osteons.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 5 (PDF p. 85)

explanations.explanation_text: A resting, inactive cell (such as a small lymphocyte or fibroyte) characteristically exhibits a small, heterochromatic, darkly stained condensed nucleus with an inconspicuous nucleolus.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 4 (PDF p. 64) & printed p. 16 (PDF p. 24)

explanations.explanation_text: Adipocytes storing triglycerides display a small, flattened, inactive eccentric nucleus compressed against the cell periphery by a single large lipid globule.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 4 (PDF p. 64)

explanations.explanation_text: A large vesicular nucleus containing abundant, unwound euchromatin (reflecting high rates of gene transcription) accompanied by a prominent, enlarged nucleolus (reflecting intense rRNA transcription and ribosome biogenesis) is the definitive cytological picture of a cell actively engaged in high-volume protein synthesis (e.g., plasma cells, pancreatic acini, growing neurons).
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 16 (PDF p. 24) & printed p. 17 (PDF p. 25)

explanations.explanation_text: A cell undergoing programmed cell death (apoptosis) shows chromatin aggregation, nuclear pyknosis, and karyorrhexis, the exact opposite of an expanded euchromatic nucleus with an active nucleolus.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 4 (PDF p. 30)

explanations.explanation_text: During metaphase, chromosomes reach maximal condensation and supercoiling, align on the equatorial plate, and are treated with mitotic inhibitors (such as colchicine) to arrest them for standard clinical karyotyping and chromosomal banding analysis.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 3 (PDF p. 33) & printed p. 7 (PDF p. 37)

explanations.explanation_text: During telophase, chromosomes arrive at the spindle poles and rapidly decondense back into fine chromatin threads within the reforming nuclear membrane.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 3 (PDF p. 33)

explanations.explanation_text: Microtubules (composed of alpha- and beta-tubulin heterodimers) form the fundamental structural backbone of both cilia and flagella, arranged in the characteristic 9+2 axonemal configuration driven by dynein ATPase arms to generate ciliary beating and flagellar propulsive motion.

explanations.explanation_text: Apoptosis is defined as a mostly physiological (and occasionally pathological), genetically controlled, energy-dependent process of programmed cell death that systematically eliminates individual scattered cells without membrane rupture or inflammatory response, essential for tissue homeostasis and embryonic morphogenesis.

explanations.explanation_text: Autolysis is post-mortem enzymatic self-digestion of dead tissues following somatic death due to the uninhibited release of intracellular lysosomal enzymes.

explanations.explanation_text: The histological constellation of individual cell shrinkage, dense nuclear chromatin aggregation (pyknosis), intact plasma membrane blebbing, and the total absence of an inflammatory response is the classic definition of apoptosis (programmed cell death).

explanations.explanation_text: In chronic gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), persistent acid and bile regurgitation damages the esophageal mucosa, inducing glandular metaplasia where the normal non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium is replaced by acid-resistant simple columnar epithelium with goblet cells (intestinal metaplasia / Barrett's esophagus).
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 5 (PDF p. 45)

explanations.explanation_text: The rough endoplasmic reticulum (rER) initiates core N-linked glycosylation, but terminal oligosaccharide trimming, extensive O-linked glycosylation, and sorting for secretion take place primarily within the Golgi apparatus.

explanations.explanation_text: The smooth endoplasmic reticulum lacks translational and protein-glycosylating machinery, synthesizing lipids and steroids instead.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 8 (PDF p. 16)

explanations.explanation_text: Ribosomes carry out polypeptide translation; they do not perform post-translational carbohydrate modifications.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 12 (PDF p. 20)

explanations.explanation_text: Aggrecan proteoglycans with their negatively charged glycosaminoglycan side chains are responsible for binding water and generating the osmotic swelling pressure that enables articular cartilage to withstand joint compression; loss or enzymatic depletion of proteoglycans leads to matrix dehydration, fibrillation, cartilage erosion, and the clinical onset of osteoarthritis.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 4 (PDF p. 77)

explanations.explanation_text: Gout is a metabolic disorder caused by hyperuricemia leading to the deposition of needle-shaped monosodium urate crystals inside joint spaces, causing acute inflammatory arthritis.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 4 (PDF p. 77)

explanations.explanation_text: The intermediate mesoderm gives rise to the kidneys, ureters, and internal reproductive organs comprising the urogenital system.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF pp. 311, 315

explanations.explanation_text: The parenchyma of the liver (hepatocytes and intrahepatic biliary epithelium) develops directly from the endodermal lining of the primitive foregut via the hepatic diverticulum.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF p. 319

explanations.explanation_text: The epidermis of the skin develops from surface ectoderm.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF p. 308

explanations.explanation_text: The central nervous system develops from neural ectoderm via the neural tube.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF pp. 304, 305

explanations.explanation_text: Skeletal muscles originate from the myotomic divisions of paraxial mesoderm somites.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF pp. 312, 314

explanations.explanation_text: This statement is factually true: the axoneme forming the core of the sperm flagellum is composed of microtubules arranged in the standard 9+2 doublet configuration.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF pp. 254, 256

explanations.explanation_text: This statement is factually true: spermatogenesis proceeds in an organized centripetal wave within the seminiferous epithelium of the testicular seminiferous tubules.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF pp. 250, 253

explanations.explanation_text: This statement is factually true: adjacent Sertoli cells form tight junctions (zonulae occludentes) near their bases that establish the immunological blood-testis barrier.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF p. 253

explanations.explanation_text: The acrosome (acrosomal cap) is derived from the Golgi apparatus (which forms the acrosomal vesicle containing hyaluronidase and acrosin); mitochondria assemble around the flagellar axoneme in the middle piece, not the acrosome.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF pp. 254, 255, 256

explanations.explanation_text: Simple squamous epithelium lines blood vessels (endothelium) and serous cavities (mesothelium), lacking the thickness and stretchability required for urinary passages.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 2 (PDF p. 42)

explanations.explanation_text: Stratified columnar epithelium is a rare epithelium found only in small areas of the male urethra and large glandular ducts, not lining the urinary tract.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 6 (PDF p. 46)

explanations.explanation_text: Transitional epithelium (urothelium) is the specialized stratified distensible epithelium that lines the urinary passages (renal calyces, renal pelvis, ureter, urinary bladder, and proximal urethra), equipped with umbrella cells that change shape reversibly between relaxed (6–8 layers) and distended (2–3 layers) states.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 6 (PDF p. 46)

explanations.explanation_text: Pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium lines the conducting portions of the respiratory system (nasal cavity, trachea, bronchi).
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 4 (PDF p. 44)

explanations.explanation_text: The erectile tissue of the penis contains vascular cavernous spaces (corpora cavernosa) lined by endothelium, but does not represent hepatic/splenic sinusoidal capillaries.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF p. 209

explanations.explanation_text: The liver is intensely rich in sinusoidal blood capillaries (hepatic sinusoids) that course between cords of hepatocytes, featuring wide, irregularly dilated lumina, discontinuous basements membranes, and fenestrations that facilitate maximal metabolic exchange between sinusoidal blood and the Space of Disse.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF pp. 199, 208

explanations.explanation_text: The tongue is composed of interlacing skeletal muscle fibers and lamina propria supplied by continuous somatic blood capillaries.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF pp. 174, 208

explanations.explanation_text: The dermis of the skin is vascularized by continuous somatic capillary loops supplying dermal papillae, not sinusoids.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF pp. 106, 208

explanations.explanation_text: Streptomycin is an aminoglycoside used for tuberculosis, tularemia, and plague, not rheumatic fever.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 41 (PDF p. 44)

explanations.explanation_text: The osteoclast is the large, multinucleated bone-resorbing cell derived from monocyte-macrophage precursors that seals against the bone surface via a ruffled border and secretes hydrochloric acid (via carbonic anhydrase) and cathepsin K to demineralize and digest the bone extracellular matrix.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 4 (PDF p. 84)

explanations.explanation_text: Osteoblasts are bone-forming cells responsible for the synthesis, deposition, and mineralization of osteoid matrix.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 3 (PDF p. 83)

explanations.explanation_text: Chondrocytes are cartilage cells that maintain cartilage matrix and do not resorb bone.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 3 (PDF p. 76)

explanations.explanation_text: Carbohydrates on the outer cell surface exist as glycoproteins and glycolipids (glycocalyx), mediating cell identity, recognition, and adhesion.
explanations.source_document: NS 101 2027 part(1) Bio.pdf, printed pp. 5, 14 (PDF pp. 7, 16); NS 101 2027 part (2) physio.pdf, printed p. 12 (PDF p. 15)

explanations.explanation_text: Triglycerides (neutral fats) function as intracellular stored energy droplets in adipose tissue and are not structural components of cell membranes.
explanations.source_document: NS 101 2027 part(1) Bio.pdf, printed p. 19 (PDF p. 21)

explanations.explanation_text: While the membrane bilayer contains phospholipids and cholesterol, 'lipid' generally does not specify the surface-coating recognition components, and glycoproteins form the major peripheral cell surface coat.
explanations.source_document: NS 101 2027 part(1) Bio.pdf, printed p. 14 (PDF p. 16)

explanations.explanation_text: Glycoprotein is a correct, well-documented answer.
explanations.source_document: NS 101 2027 part(1) Bio.pdf, printed p. 14 (PDF p. 16)

explanations.explanation_text: A pivot (trochoid) synovial joint permits axial rotation around a longitudinal axis, exemplified by the superior and inferior radioulnar joints and the median atlantoaxial joint.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF pp. 157, 159

explanations.explanation_text: The elbow joint (specifically the humeroulnar and humeroradial articulations) is the classic anatomical example of a uniaxial hinge (ginglymus) synovial joint, where the spool-like trochlea of the humerus fits into the trochlear notch of the ulna to permit movements strictly in a transverse axis: flexion and extension.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF pp. 157, 159

explanations.explanation_text: A saddle (sellar) synovial joint features reciprocally concavo-convex surfaces, exemplified by the first carpometacarpal joint of the thumb.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF pp. 157, 160

explanations.explanation_text: An ellipsoid (condyloid) joint is a biaxial joint permitting angular movements without rotation, exemplified by the radiocarpal (wrist) joint.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF pp. 157, 160

explanations.explanation_text: Each microvillus is structurally reinforced by an internal core bundle of 20 to 30 parallel actin microfilaments (fine strands 5–7 nm in diameter) anchored at the apex and inserting basally into the apical terminal web (spectrin-actin complex) to maintain rigidity and dynamic contractility.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 14 (PDF p. 22) & printed p. 5 (PDF p. 57)

explanations.explanation_text: Microtubules form the structural core axoneme of motile cilia and flagella, not microvilli.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 13–14 (PDF pp. 21–22)

explanations.explanation_text: Intermediate filaments (such as cytokeratins) insert into desmosomes and hemidesmosomes to resist cellular shearing, but do not form the internal longitudinal core of microvilli.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 14–15 (PDF pp. 22–23) & printed p. 3 (PDF p. 55)

explanations.explanation_text: Myosin thick filaments are motor proteins found in muscle sarcomeres and the terminal web; they interact with actin but do not constitute the internal structural core bundle of microvilli.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 14 (PDF p. 22) & printed p. 5 (PDF p. 57)

explanations.explanation_text: The rough endoplasmic reticulum (rER) synthesizes plasma proteins (such as albumin and clotting factors) and is not induced by lipophilic sedative drugs.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 7 (PDF p. 15)

explanations.explanation_text: Mitochondria generate ATP via oxidative phosphorylation and do not proliferate in response to microsomal drug induction.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 6 (PDF p. 14)

explanations.explanation_text: Lysosomes digest particulate matter and autophagic vacuoles, not metabolizing lipophilic therapeutic drugs.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 10 (PDF p. 18)

explanations.explanation_text: Barbiturates (such as phenobarbital) induce the rapid transcriptional upregulation and extensive morphological proliferation of the smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER) in hepatocytes, expanding its membranes and cytochrome P450 enzyme complexes to accelerate drug oxidation and detoxification.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 8 (PDF p. 16)

explanations.explanation_text: Osteomalacia is defective mineralization of the organic bone matrix (osteoid) in adults caused by vitamin D deficiency or phosphate wasting, affecting bone rather than cartilage proteoglycans.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 3 (PDF p. 83) & printed p. 7 (PDF p. 87)

explanations.explanation_text: Rheumatoid arthritis is a systemic autoimmune disease primarily initiated by synovial inflammation (synovitis) and pannus formation, not primary intrinsic degradation of articular proteoglycans.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 4 (PDF p. 77)

explanations.explanation_text: The outermost extraembryonic fetal membrane is the chorion, consisting of trophoblast and somatic extraembryonic mesoderm.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF p. 285

explanations.explanation_text: The decidua is the functional layer of the gravid uterine endometrium that has undergone extensive decidual reaction following blastocyst implantation, which provides nutrition, immune protection, and a controlled cleavage plane during parturition.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, PDF p. 280

explanations.explanation_text: Galactose is an aldohexose monosaccharide, not a sugar acid.
explanations.source_document: NS 101 2027 part(1) Bio.pdf, printed p. 5 (PDF p. 7)

explanations.explanation_text: L-ascorbic acid (Vitamin C) is a sugar acid formed from glucose in some animals (though not in humans).

explanations.explanation_text: Fructose is a ketohexose monosaccharide, not a sugar acid.
explanations.source_document: NS 101 2027 part(1) Bio.pdf, printed p. 6 (PDF p. 8)

explanations.explanation_text: Dulcitol is a sugar alcohol (polyol) produced by the reduction of galactose, not a sugar acid.

explanations.explanation_text: The primary center of endochondral ossification appears in the center of the diaphysis (the shaft) of the hyaline cartilage model during embryonic life (around the 8th week), initiating bone collar formation, cartilage calcification, and marrow cavity establishment.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 6 (PDF p. 86)

explanations.explanation_text: The epiphyseal plate is the cartilaginous growth zone situated between the epiphysis and diaphysis responsible for longitudinal bone growth, ossifying only at skeletal maturity.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 6 (PDF p. 86)

explanations.explanation_text: The epiphyseal plate is the cartilaginous growth zone situated between the epiphysis and diaphysis responsible for longitudinal bone growth, ossifying only at skeletal maturity.

explanations.explanation_text: Articular cartilage persists permanently capping synovial joint surfaces and does not undergo ossification under physiological conditions.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 6 (PDF p. 86)

explanations.explanation_text: The cytoskeleton is an intricate intracellular structural network composed entirely of protein filaments and polymers, subdivided into microtubules (tubulin polymers, 24 nm), microfilaments (actin filaments, 5–7 nm), and intermediate filaments (8–10 nm) linked together by accessory bridging proteins to establish cellular shape and enable motility. Incorrect: Nucleoproteins are complexes of nucleic acids (DNA or RNA) with proteins, such as chromatin and ribosomes, whereas the cytoskeleton is composed strictly of structural protein polymers without nucleic acid components.

explanations.explanation_text: The radial artery follows a relatively straight course along the lateral side of the forearm, lacking significant tortuosity.

explanations.explanation_text: The renal artery is an end artery passing directly and laterally from the abdominal aorta to the renal hilum, not a tortuous artery.

explanations.explanation_text: The uterine artery is a classic wavy (tortuous) artery supplying an expansile organ; its marked helical tortuosity allows it to stretch and elongate progressively without arterial compromise as the uterus enlarges during pregnancy.

explanations.explanation_text: Bilateral renal agenesis (Potter's syndrome) or severe obstructive uropathy abolishes fetal urine production (micturition), which is the primary contributor to amniotic fluid volume during the second and third trimesters, directly resulting in severe oligohydramnios.

explanations.explanation_text: Maternal diabetes mellitus induces fetal hyperglycemia and osmotic polyuria, leading characteristically to excessive amniotic fluid volume (polyhydramnios), not oligohydramnios.

explanations.explanation_text: Penicillin inhibits the bacterial transpeptidase enzyme (penicillin-binding protein), thereby preventing the transpeptidation reaction and cross-linking of peptidoglycan strands during cell wall synthesis.

explanations.explanation_text: Endothelium is the specialized histological term for simple squamous epithelium lining the internal luminal surfaces of the cardiovascular system, including the endocardium of the heart and all blood and lymphatic vessels.

explanations.explanation_text: The gas-exchanging alveoli of the lung are lined by alveolar simple squamous epithelium (type I pneumocytes) rather than being designated primarily as endothelium (which lines the adjacent pulmonary capillaries).
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 2 (PDF p. 42)

explanations.explanation_text: The mucosal luminal surface of the small and large intestine is lined by simple columnar epithelium with microvilli and goblet cells, not endothelium.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 3 (PDF p. 43)

explanations.explanation_text: The lumen of the urinary bladder is lined by transitional epithelium (urothelium), which is a specialized stratified distensible epithelium.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 6 (PDF p. 46)

explanations.explanation_text: Disruption of cell membrane function is the mechanism of action of polymyxins and daptomycin.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed pp. 29, 36 (PDF pp. 32, 39)

explanations.explanation_text: Inhibition of DNA gyrase is the mechanism of fluoroquinolones.

explanations.explanation_text: Inhibition of RNA synthesis is mediated by rifampin (inhibiting bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase).

explanations.explanation_text: Ingestion of outdated, degraded tetracyclines produces toxic degradation products (epitetracycline and anhydrotetracycline) that cause proximal renal tubular dysfunction known as Fanconi syndrome (aminoaciduria, glycosuria, phosphaturia, and acidosis).
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 39 (PDF p. 42)

explanations.explanation_text: Azithromycin is a macrolide causing GI upset, ototoxicity, and QT prolongation, not Fanconi syndrome.

explanations.explanation_text: Clindamycin is notably associated with C. difficile pseudomembranous colitis, not renal tubular Fanconi syndrome.

explanations.explanation_text: Linezolid causes reversible bone marrow suppression and peripheral neuropathy, not Fanconi syndrome.

explanations.explanation_text: Bird and non-human animal schistosomes cannot establish visceral infection in man; their cercariae penetrate human skin but cannot penetrate beyond the germinal epithelial layer, being rapidly destroyed by host defenses and causing only transient allergic dermatitis (bather’s itch or swimmer’s itch).

explanations.explanation_text: Mansonella perstans is a human filarial parasite adapted to humans, inhabiting serous body cavities.

explanations.explanation_text: Schistosoma haematobium is a major human pathogen causing urinary schistosomiasis, hematuria, bladder calcification, and squamous cell bladder cancer.

explanations.explanation_text: Wuchereria bancrofti is highly pathogenic to humans, causing lymphatic obstruction, elephantiasis, and hydrocele.

explanations.explanation_text: Burkitt lymphoma has an extremely high mitotic rate and spontaneous apoptosis; benign tingible body macrophages ingest apoptotic tumor debris and are surrounded by clear halos against a dark background of basophilic neoplastic B cells, producing the classic "starry sky" histological appearance.

explanations.explanation_text: Hodgkin lymphoma is histologically characterized by diagnostic Reed-Sternberg (RS) cells in a background of reactive non-neoplastic inflammatory cells, not a starry-sky pattern.

explanations.explanation_text: Mantle cell lymphoma exhibits a diffuse or vaguely nodular effacement of the lymph node by monotonous small-to-medium lymphocytes with irregular nuclei.

explanations.explanation_text: The substitution of hydrophobic valine for hydrophilic glutamate generates protruding hydrophobic "sticky patches" on the surface of deoxy-HbS beta-subunits that bind complementary receptor sites on adjacent alpha-subunits, driving polymer formation and fiber aggregation.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (2) 2027 bio.pdf, printed p. 8 (PDF p. 10)

explanations.explanation_text: Because negative glutamate is replaced by neutral valine, HbS has a lower negative surface charge than HbA and moves more SLOWLY towards the positive anode on alkaline electrophoresis.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (2) 2027 bio.pdf, printed p. 8 (PDF p. 10)

explanations.explanation_text: Polymerized HbS has a decreased affinity for oxygen compared to normal HbA, facilitating early oxygen release and further deoxygenation-induced sickling.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (2) 2027 bio.pdf, printed p. 8 (PDF p. 10)

explanations.explanation_text: The initial and rate-limiting step of heme biosynthesis is the mitochondrial condensation of glycine and succinyl-CoA catalyzed by delta-aminolevulinate synthase (ALA synthase) in the presence of pyridoxal phosphate (PLP) to form delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA).
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (2) 2027 bio.pdf, printed p. 11 (PDF p. 13)

explanations.explanation_text: Heme allosterically INHIBITS and represses (downregulates) ALA synthase via negative feedback; it does not stimulate it.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (2) 2027 bio.pdf, printed p. 11 (PDF p. 13)

explanations.explanation_text: Lead poisoning strongly INHIBITS ferrochelatase (and ALA dehydratase) by binding to their sulfhydryl (-SH) groups, leading to accumulation of protoporphyrin in erythrocytes.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (2) 2027 bio.pdf, printed pp. 11, 12, 14 (PDF pp. 13, 14, 16)

explanations.explanation_text: Option A is INCORRECT (and thus the correct answer to this negative question): in the deoxy (T) form, the central cavity is LARGE enough to accommodate a molecule of 2,3-BPG, whereas in the oxy (R) form, the cavity becomes TOO SMALL for it.

explanations.explanation_text: This statement is correct: 2,3-BPG binding stabilizes the low-affinity T conformation and decreases the oxygen affinity of hemoglobin, shifting the dissociation curve to the right.

explanations.explanation_text: This statement is correct: 2,3-BPG binds specifically in the central water-filled cavity located at the dyad symmetry axis between the beta-globin subunits.

explanations.explanation_text: This statement is correct: erythrocyte 2,3-BPG concentration increases significantly as an adaptive mechanism during high-altitude living and chronic hypoxia.

explanations.explanation_text: Osteocytes are mature, post-mitotic bone cells that reside individually enclosed within small ellipsoidal matrix cavities called lacunae throughout mineralized compact and cancellous bone.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 3–4 (PDF pp. 83–84)

explanations.explanation_text: Osteoblasts are active, bone-forming cuboidal cells situated on the external or internal surfaces of growing or remodeling bone (under periosteum or endosteum); only when surrounded by newly calcified matrix do they differentiate into osteocytes inside lacunae.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 3 (PDF p. 83)

explanations.explanation_text: An osteon (Haversian system) is the cylindrical structural and functional unit of compact bone, not a cell residing inside a lacuna.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 5 (PDF p. 85)

explanations.explanation_text: Osteoid is the unmineralized organic extracellular matrix consisting of type I collagen and proteoglycans secreted by osteoblasts prior to calcification, not a cell type.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 3 (PDF p. 83)

explanations.explanation_text: Antigenic variation of surface coat glycoproteins (VSG) is the specialized immune evasion mechanism of African trypanosomes, not Schistosoma.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 69, 103 (PDF pp. 74, 108)

explanations.explanation_text: Cleavage of immunoglobulins by specific parasitic proteases into Fab and Fc fragments is typically documented for Trypanosoma cruzi, whereas antigen disguise with host proteins is the classic mechanism emphasized for adult Schistosoma.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 12, 103 (PDF pp. 17, 108)

explanations.explanation_text: Intracellular survival within macrophages is characteristic of Leishmania and Toxoplasma, whereas Schistosoma adult worms are large extracellular macroparasites residing inside venous blood vessels.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 77, 102 (PDF pp. 82, 107)

explanations.explanation_text: Myopathy and rhabdomyolysis are well-known adverse effects of statins; in patients presenting with muscle aches, pain, or weakness, serum creatine kinase (CK) levels should be checked immediately to evaluate for skeletal muscle damage.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 18 (PDF p. 21)

explanations.explanation_text: Serum aminotransferases (ALT/AST) monitor statin-induced hepatotoxicity, not skeletal muscle myopathy.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 18 (PDF p. 21)

explanations.explanation_text: Serum creatinine evaluates overall renal filtration, which may be checked secondarily if rhabdomyolysis is severe, but CK is the direct primary test for muscle injury.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 18 (PDF p. 21)

explanations.explanation_text: Troponin I is specific for myocardial necrosis in acute coronary syndromes, not skeletal muscle myositis.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 18 (PDF p. 21)

explanations.explanation_text: The Sabin-Feldman dye test is a complement-mediated neutralization assay: specific anti-Toxoplasma IgG antibodies in patient serum bind to surface antigens of live tachyzoites, activating complement to lyse the cell membrane so that the organisms fail to take up methylene blue dye (positive result).
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 61 (PDF p. 66)

explanations.explanation_text: Although endoderm gives rise to extensive epithelial surfaces (such as the epithelial lining of the gastrointestinal and respiratory tracts and parenchymal organs), it is not the sole source of epithelium.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 1 (PDF p. 41) & PDF p. 319

explanations.explanation_text: Although mesoderm gives rise to vascular endothelium, serosal mesothelium, and the urogenital epithelium, epithelium is also derived from ectoderm and endoderm.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 1 (PDF p. 41) & PDF p. 315

explanations.explanation_text: Although mesoderm gives rise to vascular endothelium, serosal mesothelium, and the urogenital epithelium, epithelium is also derived from ectoderm and endoderm.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 1 (PDF p. 41) & PDF p. 308

explanations.explanation_text: Epithelial tissue is uniquely derived from all three embryonic germ layers: ectoderm (forms epidermis, oral and anal mucosa), mesoderm (forms endothelium, mesothelium, and urinary tract lining), and endoderm (forms lining of the GI tract, respiratory tree, and associated glandular parenchyma).
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 1 (PDF p. 41)

explanations.explanation_text: While minor liver function abnormalities may occur, severe life-threatening bone marrow hematotoxicity is the hallmark toxic effect of ticlopidine.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 12 (PDF p. 15)

explanations.explanation_text: Tinnitus is a classic symptom of salicylism (aspirin toxicity) and cinchonism (quinine toxicity), not ticlopidine.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 11 (PDF p. 14)

explanations.explanation_text: The inner mitochondrial membrane is extensively folded inward into shelf-like or tubular projections called cristae, which dramatically increase the available surface area for respiratory electron transport chain complexes and ATP synthase particles.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 6 (PDF p. 14)

explanations.explanation_text: A desmosome (macula adherens) is an intercellular adhering junction providing mechanical attachment between adjacent epithelial cells, unrelated to mitochondrial structure.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 3 (PDF p. 55)

explanations.explanation_text: A cistern (cisterna) is a flattened fluid-filled membranous sac found in the endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi complex, not the folds of inner mitochondrial membranes.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 7 (PDF p. 15) & printed p. 9 (PDF p. 17)

explanations.explanation_text: The mitochondrial matrix is the gel-like aqueous compartment enclosed by the inner mitochondrial membrane containing enzymes of the citric acid cycle, ribosomes, and mtDNA, not the membranous projections themselves.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 7 (PDF p. 15)

explanations.explanation_text: Bradycardia is not an established side effect of ticlopidine.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 12 (PDF p. 15)

explanations.explanation_text: Ticlopidine causes severe neutropenia (agranulocytosis) in approximately 1% of patients, as well as thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP), which severely restricts its clinical use in favor of clopidogrel.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 12 (PDF p. 15)

explanations.explanation_text: Repeated acute episodes of retrograde lymphangitis and lymphadenitis accompanied by elephantoid fever define the acute inflammatory stage of filariasis.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 22 (PDF p. 27)

explanations.explanation_text: The chronic obstructive stage of Wuchereria bancrofti infection results from long-standing lymphatic stasis and fibroblast proliferation, leading to brawny non-pitting edema (elephantiasis) and thickened, rough, fissured hyperkeratotic skin changes.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 23, 24 (PDF pp. 28, 29)

explanations.explanation_text: Tropical pulmonary eosinophilia (TPE) is an occult, hypersensitivity-mediated manifestation where microfilariae are destroyed in pulmonary capillaries, not the standard chronic obstructive peripheral stage.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 24, 25 (PDF pp. 29, 30)

explanations.explanation_text: In the chronic obstructive stage, microfilariae typically disappear from the peripheral blood; furthermore, W. bancrofti exhibits nocturnal (not diurnal) periodicity.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 21, 26 (PDF pp. 26, 31)

explanations.explanation_text: Sandy patches and urinary bladder calculi are characteristic manifestations of chronic urinary schistosomiasis caused by Schistosoma haematobium.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 10 (PDF p. 15)

explanations.explanation_text: In the late chronic stage of S. japonicum (and S. mansoni), embolization of eggs to the intrahepatic portal venules elicits granulomatous inflammation, periportal (Symmers) pipestem fibrosis, portal hypertension, splenomegaly, ascites, and bleeding esophageal varices.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 10, 11, 15 (PDF pp. 15, 16, 20)

explanations.explanation_text: Immune-complex-mediated acute febrile illness is Katayama syndrome (type III hypersensitivity), which occurs during the early acute stage (4 to 8 weeks after infection).
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 9, 15 (PDF pp. 14, 20)

explanations.explanation_text: Cercarial dermatitis and transient papular skin rash occur during the initial invasion stage within 1 to 4 days of cercarial skin penetration.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 8 (PDF p. 13)

explanations.explanation_text: In Plasmodium vivax, the young trophozoite (early ring stage) is large, measures approximately one-third of the diameter of the enlarged host erythrocyte, and has a delicate cytoplasmic rim with a chromatin dot.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 37 (PDF p. 42)

explanations.explanation_text: Multiple ring forms inside a single red blood cell and accolé (marginal) forms are classic hallmarks of Plasmodium falciparum, not P. vivax.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 37 (PDF p. 42)

explanations.explanation_text: Goblet cells are specialized mucus-secreting unicellular exocrine glands that are prominently and characteristically interspersed among ciliated columnar cells in the respiratory epithelium (pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium) of the trachea.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 3–4 (PDF pp. 43–44)

explanations.explanation_text: The esophagus is lined by non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium, which entirely lacks goblet cells; its lubrication is provided by submucosal esophageal glands.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 5 (PDF p. 45)

explanations.explanation_text: The oral cavity is lined by stratified squamous epithelium (keratinized or non-keratinized) lubricated by major and minor salivary glands, containing no goblet cells.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 5 (PDF p. 45)

explanations.explanation_text: The urinary bladder is lined by transitional epithelium (urothelium) composed of umbrella/dome-shaped surface cells, without goblet cells.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 6 (PDF p. 46)

explanations.explanation_text: During metaphase, the nuclear envelope has already completely disassembled and double-stranded chromosomes are aligned along the equatorial metaphase plate attached to mitotic spindle fibers.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 3 (PDF p. 33)

explanations.explanation_text: During prophase (the first stage of mitosis), chromatin condenses into distinct chromosomes, the centrioles migrate to opposite poles, and both the nucleolus and nuclear envelope disassemble and disappear.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 3 (PDF p. 33)

explanations.explanation_text: During anaphase, centromeres split and sister chromatids separate to migrate toward opposite spindle poles, occurring after nuclear envelope disappearance.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 3 (PDF p. 33)

explanations.explanation_text: During telophase, the nuclear envelope and nucleoli reassemble around the separated chromosomes at each pole, which is the reappearance rather than disappearance of the nucleus.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 3 (PDF p. 33)

explanations.explanation_text: Crescent- or banana-shaped gametocytes are unique to Plasmodium falciparum; P. vivax gametocytes are spherical/rounded and fill the enlarged RBC.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 37 (PDF p. 42)

explanations.explanation_text: Plasmodium vivax does produce dormant liver hypnozoites, which are responsible for late true relapses of benign tertian malaria.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 35, 40 (PDF pp. 40, 45)

explanations.explanation_text: Lumbar puncture and CSF examination are mandatory in African trypanosomiasis for disease staging (detecting trypanosomes, elevated protein, morula cells, and pleocytosis).
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 70 (PDF p. 75)

explanations.explanation_text: Option B is the correct exam answer because Plasmodium vivax causes benign tertian malaria without CNS tropism; diagnosis is made by peripheral blood examination, and CSF examination plays no role.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 45, 106 (PDF pp. 50, 111)

explanations.explanation_text: CSF examination is a key diagnostic method in Acanthamoeba granulomatous amoebic encephalitis (GAE) to detect trophozoites, cysts, and lymphocytic pleocytosis.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 93, 95 (PDF pp. 98, 100)

explanations.explanation_text: CSF wet mounts and Giemsa staining are the primary definitive tests to visualize motile Naegleria fowleri trophozoites in acute PAM.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 86, 95 (PDF pp. 91, 100)

explanations.explanation_text: Erythrocytes parasitized by mature stages of P. falciparum develop surface knobs expressing PfEMP-1, which mediate cytoadherence to capillary endothelium and resetting, causing sequestration in deep microvasculature (brain, kidneys, gut).
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 42 (PDF p. 47)

explanations.explanation_text: Selective infection restricted to older, senescent RBCs is characteristic of Plasmodium malariae; P. falciparum invades red blood cells of any age.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 41 (PDF p. 46)

explanations.explanation_text: Plasmodium falciparum does NOT form liver hypnozoites and therefore does not cause true relapses; clinical recurrences represent recrudescence of persistent sub-patent erythrocytic forms.

explanations.explanation_text: Direct thrombin inhibitors (such as parenteral argatroban, lepirudin, and oral dabigatran) bind directly to the active catalytic site of thrombin independent of antithrombin III and are used as non-heparin alternatives when managing heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT).

explanations.explanation_text: Gemfibrozil is a fibrate (PPAR-alpha agonist) whose primary and profound therapeutic effect is lowering plasma triglycerides (TGs) by activating lipoprotein lipase and stimulating hepatic fatty acid oxidation, with minimal or no effect in lowering LDL cholesterol.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 20 (PDF p. 23)

explanations.explanation_text: The Golgi apparatus is the dedicated secretory apparatus of the cell; it receives newly synthesized proteins from the rER, performs post-translational modifications (glycosylation, sulfation, phosphorylation), concentrates them, and packages them into mature secretory vesicles for regulated or constitutive exocytosis.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 8–9 (PDF pp. 16–17)

explanations.explanation_text: Lysosomes are membrane-bound digestive organelles containing acid hydrolytic enzymes dedicated to intracellular degradation (heterophagy, autophagy, and autolysis), not export secretion.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 9–10 (PDF pp. 17–18)

explanations.explanation_text: The smooth endoplasmic reticulum (sER) lacks ribosomes and participates in lipid/steroid biosynthesis, glycogen metabolism, calcium sequestration, and drug detoxification, rather than packaging secretory proteins.
explanations.source_document: Normal Structure II Handout, printed p. 8 (PDF p. 16)

explanations.explanation_text: Cholestyramine is a bile acid sequestrant that selectively lowers LDL cholesterol; it has no triglyceride-lowering effect and can even raise plasma triglycerides.

explanations.explanation_text: Colesevelam is a bile acid sequestrant resin acting exclusively to lower LDL-cholesterol.

explanations.explanation_text: Ezetimibe selectively inhibits cholesterol absorption at the brush border, reducing LDL cholesterol without meaningful impact on triglycerides.

explanations.explanation_text: T. b. rhodesiense is MUCH MORE virulent than T. b. gambiense, causing an acute, fulminant disease course with early death.

explanations.explanation_text: In East African trypanosomiasis (T. b. rhodesiense), lymphadenopathy and Winterbottom’s sign are characteristically LESS prominent than in T. b. gambiense, while myocarditis and fulminant toxemia predominate.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 68 (PDF p. 73)

explanations.explanation_text: A long chronic course lasting years is characteristic of T. b. gambiense (West African sleeping sickness); rhodesiense leads to death within 9 to 12 months.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 68 (PDF p. 73)

explanations.explanation_text: Transmission near rivers and lakes by riverine tsetse flies (Glossina palpalis) occurs in gambiense; rhodesiense is transmitted in savannah woodland/jungle by Glossina morsitans.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 68 (PDF p. 73)

explanations.explanation_text: PCSK9 inhibitors (evolocumab, alirocumab) prevent PCSK9 from targeting the LDL receptor for lysosomal degradation, thereby preserving and increasing cell-surface LDL receptors to enhance hepatic LDL clearance from the bloodstream.

explanations.explanation_text: Inhibition of de novo cholesterol biosynthesis is the mechanism of statins (HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors), not PCSK9 antibodies.

explanations.explanation_text: Decreased intestinal wall cholesterol absorption is mediated by ezetimibe.

explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 19 (PDF p. 22)

explanations.explanation_text: Successive cyclical waves of parasitemia in African trypanosomiasis are caused by antigenic variation of the Variable Surface Glycoprotein (VSG) coat, allowing emerging variable antigenic types (VATs) to escape host humoral antibodies every 7 to 14 days.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 69, 103 (PDF pp. 74, 108)

explanations.explanation_text: Low-molecular-weight heparins (LMWH) have high subcutaneous bioavailability, predictable dose-response pharmacokinetics, and do not non-specifically bind plasma proteins or endothelial cells, so routine laboratory coagulation monitoring (aPTT) is not required.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 6 (PDF p. 9)

explanations.explanation_text: LMWH has a significantly LOWER risk of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) compared to unfractionated heparin.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed pp. 5, 6 (PDF pp. 8, 9)

explanations.explanation_text: LMWH has a LONGER plasma half-life (allowing once- or twice-daily subcutaneous dosing) compared to UFH (which has a short half-life of 2-4 hours).
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed pp. 5, 6 (PDF pp. 8, 9)

explanations.explanation_text: LMWH is administered predominantly by the subcutaneous (SC) route, not IV only.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 6 (PDF p. 9)

explanations.explanation_text: Alteplase (recombinant tissue plasminogen activator, t-PA) is fibrin-specific: it has little enzymatic activity unless bound to fibrin within a thrombus, resulting in localized clot lysis with minimal systemic plasminogen activation and lower danger of widespread lytic bleeding.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 13 (PDF p. 16)

explanations.explanation_text: Streptokinase is a non-fibrin-selective thrombolytic agent that binds free and bound plasminogen indiscriminately, causing widespread systemic fibrinogen breakdown and higher bleeding risk.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 13 (PDF p. 16)

explanations.explanation_text: Urokinase directly converts free and bound plasminogen into plasmin without selective affinity for fibrin.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed pp. 13, 14 (PDF pp. 16, 17)

explanations.explanation_text: Aminocaproic acid is an antifibrinolytic inhibitor that prevents plasminogen activation; it is not a thrombolytic agent.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 14 (PDF p. 17)

explanations.explanation_text: Aminocaproic acid (and tranexamic acid) competitively inhibits plasminogen activation and fibrin binding, acting as a specific antidote to treat life-threatening bleeding resulting from thrombolytic/fibrinolytic overdose.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 14 (PDF p. 17)

explanations.explanation_text: Fresh frozen plasma can replenish depleted clotting factors supportive of hemostasis, but the specific pharmacological fibrinolytic inhibitor antidote is aminocaproic acid.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 14 (PDF p. 17)

explanations.explanation_text: Protamine sulfate is the specific chemical antidote used to neutralize heparin, having no inhibitory effect on streptokinase or plasmin.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 6 (PDF p. 9)

explanations.explanation_text: Vitamin K is the reversal agent for warfarin; it has no acute inhibitory effect against circulating active plasmin generated by streptokinase.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 9 (PDF p. 12)

explanations.explanation_text: Sodium stibogluconate (Pentostam), a pentavalent antimony compound administered IV or IM at 20 mg/kg/day for 20-30 days, is the classical first-line drug of choice for visceral leishmaniasis (Kala-azar) in endemic areas.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 82 (PDF p. 87)

explanations.explanation_text: Metronidazole is an antiprotozoal drug active against anaerobic protozoa (Entamoeba histolytica, Giardia lamblia, Trichomonas vaginalis) and anaerobes, with no efficacy in Kala-azar.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 44 (PDF p. 47)

explanations.explanation_text: Chloroquine is an antimalarial blood schizonticide with no activity against Leishmania amastigotes.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 47 (PDF p. 52)

explanations.explanation_text: Praziquantel is an anthelmintic agent used for schistosomiasis and tapeworms, having no antiprotozoal activity.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 14, 15 (PDF pp. 19, 20)

explanations.explanation_text: Burkitt cells are neoplastic medium-sized mature B lymphocytes characteristic of Burkitt non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (3) 2027 pathology.pdf, printed p. 11 (PDF p. 12)

explanations.explanation_text: Burkitt cells are neoplastic medium-sized mature B lymphocytes characteristic of Burkitt non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (3) 2027 pathology.pdf, printed pp. 14, 16 (PDF pp. 15, 17)

explanations.explanation_text: Sézary cells are neoplastic T cells with cerebriform nuclei characteristic of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (Mycosis fungoides / Sézary syndrome).
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (3) 2027 pathology.pdf, printed p. 12 (PDF p. 13)

explanations.explanation_text: Mantle cells are the malignant lymphoid elements of mantle cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (3) 2027 pathology.pdf, printed p. 8 (PDF p. 9)

explanations.explanation_text: Primary lymphoma typically presents with generalized or painless rubbery lymphadenopathy and systemic B symptoms, but hemoptysis indicates a pulmonary parenchymal primary lesion (such as bronchogenic carcinoma) draining to supraclavicular/cervical nodes.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (3) 2027 pathology.pdf, printed pp. 3, 13 (PDF pp. 4, 14)

explanations.explanation_text: Hemoptysis suggests a primary lung cancer that has metastasized to the regional and deep cervical/supraclavicular lymph nodes; metastatic carcinoma is a frequent cause of firm, fixed cervical lymph node enlargement in patients with primary respiratory tumors.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (3) 2027 pathology.pdf, printed pp. 3, 5 (PDF pp. 4, 6)

explanations.explanation_text: Absence of IgM strongly argues against acute primary infection, as IgM appears rapidly within 1-2 weeks of acute exposure.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 61 (PDF p. 66)

explanations.explanation_text: Acute bacterial lymphadenitis presents with painful, warm, red, tender regional nodes draining an acute head and neck infection (e.g. tonsillitis), not chronic hemoptysis.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (3) 2027 pathology.pdf, printed pp. 3, 4 (PDF pp. 4, 5)

explanations.explanation_text: Although TB can cause hemoptysis and scrofula, metastatic malignant disease is the primary diagnostic entity tested when evaluating neoplastic cervical lymph node enlargement secondary to lung signs.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (3) 2027 pathology.pdf, printed pp. 3, 5 (PDF pp. 4, 6)

explanations.explanation_text: Follicular lymphoma is a B-cell Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma (accounting for ~40% of adult NHLs) characterized by t(14;18) translocation involving BCL2.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (3) 2027 pathology.pdf, printed pp. 8, 9 (PDF pp. 9, 10)

explanations.explanation_text: Nodular sclerosis is the most common subtype of classical Hodgkin lymphoma.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (3) 2027 pathology.pdf, printed pp. 13, 15 (PDF pp. 14, 16)

explanations.explanation_text: Mixed cellularity is the second most common histological subtype of classical Hodgkin lymphoma.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (3) 2027 pathology.pdf, printed pp. 13, 15 (PDF pp. 14, 16)

explanations.explanation_text: Lymphocyte depletion is an uncommon, aggressive subtype of classical Hodgkin lymphoma.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (3) 2027 pathology.pdf, printed pp. 13, 15 (PDF pp. 14, 16)

explanations.explanation_text: Cell wall synthesis inhibition is mediated by beta-lactam antibiotics and glycopeptides.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 29 (PDF p. 32)

explanations.explanation_text: Aminoglycosides irreversibly bind to the 30S ribosomal subunit, causing misreading of the mRNA template (incorporation of incorrect amino acids into growing peptide chains) and blocking translocation, resulting in nonfunctional and toxic bacterial proteins.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 40 (PDF p. 43)

explanations.explanation_text: Inhibition of DNA gyrase is the bactericidal mechanism of fluoroquinolones.

explanations.explanation_text: Direct disruption of bacterial cell membrane integrity is the mechanism of daptomycin and polymyxins.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed pp. 29, 36 (PDF pp. 32, 39)

explanations.explanation_text: Ciprofloxacin and other fluoroquinolones can cause tendinitis and tendon rupture (most commonly affecting the Achilles tendon), especially in elderly patients and those receiving concomitant systemic corticosteroids.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 51 (PDF p. 54)

explanations.explanation_text: Gray baby syndrome is caused by chloramphenicol toxicity in premature and newborn infants.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 45 (PDF p. 48)

explanations.explanation_text: Ototoxicity is characteristically produced by aminoglycosides (gentamicin, streptomycin) and vancomycin.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed pp. 36, 41 (PDF pp. 39, 44)

explanations.explanation_text: Gray baby syndrome is caused by chloramphenicol toxicity in premature and newborn infants.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 36 (PDF p. 39)

explanations.explanation_text: Viral infections characteristically stimulate lymphocytosis and monocytosis, not peripheral blood eosinophilia.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (3) 2027 pathology.pdf, printed p. 2 (PDF p. 3)

explanations.explanation_text: Acute bacterial infections classically induce neutrophilic leukocytosis.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (3) 2027 pathology.pdf, printed p. 2 (PDF p. 3)

explanations.explanation_text: Peripheral eosinophilia is a classic diagnostic hallmark of invasive tissue parasitic infections (especially helminthic infections like Schistosoma, Wuchereria bancrofti, Fasciola, and Trichinella) mediated by IL-5 and IgE-dependent mechanisms.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 97, 101 (PDF pp. 102, 106)

explanations.explanation_text: Fungal infections evoke primarily granulomatous and neutrophilic immune responses without striking eosinophilia.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 51 (PDF p. 54)

explanations.explanation_text: Penicillins inhibit the bacterial transpeptidase enzyme (penicillin-binding protein), preventing the transpeptidation reaction that establishes peptide cross-linkages between adjacent glycan chains in the bacterial peptidoglycan cell wall.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 30 (PDF p. 33)

explanations.explanation_text: The 50S ribosomal subunit is targeted by macrolides, chloramphenicol, and clindamycin, not beta-lactams.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed pp. 37, 42, 44 (PDF pp. 40, 45, 47)

explanations.explanation_text: DNA topoisomerase IV is targeted by fluoroquinolones.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 48 (PDF p. 51)

explanations.explanation_text: Folic acid biosynthesis is inhibited by sulfonamides and trimethoprim.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 46 (PDF p. 49)

explanations.explanation_text: High avidity IgG indicates that antibody maturation occurred past months ago, confirming past, chronic, or latent infection contracted at least 3-5 months earlier.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 61 (PDF p. 66)

explanations.explanation_text: Low avidity anti-Toxoplasma IgG antibodies denote recently produced antibodies that have not yet undergone somatic hypermutation and affinity maturation; presence of low avidity IgG (often along with IgM) is a specific diagnostic indicator of recent acute infection.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 61 (PDF p. 66)

explanations.explanation_text: Aspirin potentiates the bleeding risk of anticoagulants via antiplatelet action and displacement of warfarin from plasma protein binding sites.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 8 (PDF p. 11)

explanations.explanation_text: Estrogen-containing oral contraceptives stimulate hepatic synthesis of vitamin K-dependent clotting factors (factors II, VII, IX, X), antagonizing and reducing the anticoagulant efficacy of oral anticoagulants like warfarin.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 9 (PDF p. 12)

explanations.explanation_text: Cimetidine is a microsomal enzyme inhibitor that increases the anticoagulant action of warfarin, elevating the INR and bleeding risk.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 9 (PDF p. 12)

explanations.explanation_text: Amiodarone inhibits warfarin metabolism via CYP2C9, significantly potentiating warfarin anticoagulant action.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 8 (PDF p. 11)

explanations.explanation_text: Clopidogrel is an irreversible antagonist of the platelet P2Y12 ADP receptor, not a direct GP IIb/IIIa antagonist.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 12 (PDF p. 15)

explanations.explanation_text: Ticagrelor is a reversible direct antagonist of the platelet P2Y12 ADP receptor.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 12 (PDF p. 15)

explanations.explanation_text: Abciximab (spelled Aciximab in the exam) is a chimeric monoclonal antibody Fab fragment that directly and reversibly blocks the platelet glycoprotein IIb/IIIa integrin receptor, preventing fibrinogen binding and platelet aggregation.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed pp. 11, 12 (PDF pp. 14, 15)

explanations.explanation_text: Heparin is an indirect thrombin inhibitor that activates antithrombin III; it is not an antiplatelet GP IIb/IIIa antagonist.

explanations.explanation_text: This statement is correct: hemoglobin is a tetramer composed of four globin polypeptide chains.
