explanations.explanation_text: Option B is INCORRECT (and thus the correct answer to this negative question): each globin chain binds exactly ONE heme molecule; the entire hemoglobin tetramer contains a total of four heme molecules, not 4 heme per chain.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (2) 2027 bio.pdf, printed pp. 1, 3 (PDF pp. 3, 5)

explanations.explanation_text: This statement is correct: the iron atom in functional hemoglobin must remain in the reduced ferrous (Fe2+) state to reversibly bind molecular oxygen.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (2) 2027 bio.pdf, printed pp. 1, 4 (PDF pp. 3, 6)

explanations.explanation_text: This statement is correct: adult hemoglobin (HbA) consists of two alpha and two beta polypeptide chains (alpha2beta2).
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (2) 2027 bio.pdf, printed p. 3 (PDF p. 5)

explanations.explanation_text: Prothrombin time (PT/INR) is primarily used to monitor oral anticoagulant therapy with warfarin, which affects extrinsic pathway factor VII.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 8 (PDF p. 11)

explanations.explanation_text: Unfractionated heparin inhibits the intrinsic and common coagulation pathways (factors XIIa, XIa, IXa, Xa, and IIa); therapeutic anticoagulation is routinely monitored and dosage adjusted using the activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT), with a therapeutic target of 2.0 to 2.5 times the control baseline.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed pp. 5, 8 (PDF pp. 8, 11)

explanations.explanation_text: Bleeding time assesses primary platelet plug formation and is affected by antiplatelet agents (aspirin) or thrombocytopenia, not routinely prolonged by heparin.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 1 (PDF p. 4)

explanations.explanation_text: Prothrombin time (PT/INR) is primarily used to monitor oral anticoagulant therapy with warfarin, which affects extrinsic pathway factor VII.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 5 (PDF p. 8)

explanations.explanation_text: G6PD deficiency impairs NADPH production and glutathione reduction, making red cells susceptible to oxidative hemolysis.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (2) 2027 bio.pdf, printed p. 16 (PDF p. 18)

explanations.explanation_text: Accelerated peripheral destruction of red cells triggers compensatory erythropoietin release and robust bone marrow reticulocytosis.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 46 (PDF p. 51)

explanations.explanation_text: Option C is the correct exam answer because it is FALSE: deficiency of galactose-1-phosphate uridylyltransferase causes classical galactosemia, not hemolytic anemia.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (2) 2027 bio.pdf, printed p. 16 (PDF p. 18)

explanations.explanation_text: Massive degradation of heme from hemolyzed erythrocytes produces excessive unconjugated (indirect) hyperbilirubinemia.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (2) 2027 bio.pdf, printed pp. 15, 16 (PDF pp. 17, 18)

explanations.explanation_text: This is correct: 2,3-BPG binds specifically in the central cavity between beta-globin chains of deoxyhemoglobin.

explanations.explanation_text: This is correct: 2,3-BPG synthesis increases during chronic hypoxia and high altitude to facilitate tissue oxygen delivery.

explanations.explanation_text: This is true: mature schizonts rupture infected red blood cells, releasing merozoites, pigments, and toxins into the blood.

explanations.explanation_text: Option D is the INCORRECT statement (and therefore the correct answer): the erythrocytic cycle is an ASEXUAL cycle (schizogony or merogony); sexual reproduction (sporogony) takes place exclusively in the mosquito vector.

explanations.explanation_text: In Giemsa-stained thin blood smears of malaria, characteristic intraerythrocytic stages include band forms or "basket of trophozoites" (typical of Plasmodium malariae and developing trophozoites).

explanations.explanation_text: Amastigote nests (pseudocysts) are found in tissue biopsy sections of heart muscle in Trypanosoma cruzi or RES in Leishmania, not in Plasmodium blood smears.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 71, 77 (PDF pp. 76, 82)

explanations.explanation_text: Trypomastigote forms are diagnostic of Trypanosoma species (T. brucei, T. cruzi), not Plasmodium.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 64, 71 (PDF pp. 69, 76)

explanations.explanation_text: Promastigote rosettes are observed in NNN culture of Leishmania, not in malarial blood films.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 81 (PDF p. 86)

explanations.explanation_text: Atorvastatin inhibits intracellular hepatic HMG-CoA reductase; it does not bind or act directly upon bile in the intestinal lumen.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 17 (PDF p. 20)

explanations.explanation_text: Ezetimibe blocks the NPC1L1 sterol transporter at the enterocyte brush border to prevent cholesterol absorption, but does not bind or sequester bile acids.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 22 (PDF p. 25)

explanations.explanation_text: Cholestyramine is an anion-exchange resin that binds negatively charged bile acids in the intestinal lumen, preventing their enterohepatic reabsorption and forcing the liver to convert endogenous cholesterol into new bile acids.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 19 (PDF p. 22)

explanations.explanation_text: Niacin inhibits lipolysis in adipose tissue and reduces hepatic VLDL production; it does not act on bile acids.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 21 (PDF p. 24)

explanations.explanation_text: Iron released from heme degradation by heme oxygenase is recycled and bound to ferritin or transferrin; it is not normally excreted in urine.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (2) 2027 bio.pdf, printed p. 14 (PDF p. 16)

explanations.explanation_text: Globin polypeptide chains are proteolytically degraded into individual amino acids that enter the general amino acid pool; bile acids are synthesized from cholesterol.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (2) 2027 bio.pdf, printed p. 14 (PDF p. 16)

explanations.explanation_text: Lipid-soluble unconjugated bilirubin released by reticuloendothelial macrophages enters the circulation and is transported to hepatocytes tightly bound to plasma albumin.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (2) 2027 bio.pdf, printed pp. 14, 15 (PDF pp. 16, 17)

explanations.explanation_text: Heme cannot be reused directly; it is cleaved by microsomal heme oxygenase into biliverdin, releasing free iron (Fe2+) and carbon monoxide.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (2) 2027 bio.pdf, printed p. 14 (PDF p. 16)

explanations.explanation_text: Nodular sclerosis is the most common subtype of classical Hodgkin lymphoma.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (3) 2027 pathology.pdf, printed pp. 13, 15 (PDF pp. 14, 16)

explanations.explanation_text: Mixed cellularity is a classic subtype of Hodgkin lymphoma characterized by Reed-Sternberg cells in a pleomorphic inflammatory background.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (3) 2027 pathology.pdf, printed pp. 13, 15 (PDF pp. 14, 16)

explanations.explanation_text: Follicular lymphoma is a B-cell Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma (NHL) characterized by nodular lymphoid architecture and t(14;18) translocation.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (3) 2027 pathology.pdf, printed pp. 8, 9 (PDF pp. 9, 10)

explanations.explanation_text: Lymphocyte-rich is a subtype of classical Hodgkin lymphoma.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (3) 2027 pathology.pdf, printed pp. 13, 15 (PDF pp. 14, 16)

explanations.explanation_text: Chloroquine is a diprotic weak base that concentrates heavily inside the acidic food vacuole of the intraerythrocytic parasite, capping hemozoin polymerization.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 36 (PDF p. 41)

explanations.explanation_text: Chloroquine is widely used for suppressive chemoprophylaxis in healthy non-immune travelers visiting malaria-endemic regions without chloroquine resistance.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 47, 48 (PDF pp. 52, 53)

explanations.explanation_text: Option C is the correct exam answer because chloroquine is NOT a tissue schizonticide; it has no activity against exoerythrocytic liver stages or dormant hypnozoites (tissue schizonticides are primaquine and pyrimethamine).
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 47 (PDF p. 52)

explanations.explanation_text: Chloroquine is a highly potent blood schizonticide that rapidly terminates erythrocytic schizogony to achieve clinical cure.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 47 (PDF p. 52)

explanations.explanation_text: HbS is caused by a single point missense mutation (GAG to GTG) in the sixth codon of the beta-globin gene.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (2) 2027 bio.pdf, printed p. 8 (PDF p. 10)

explanations.explanation_text: The molecular lesion is the replacement of hydrophilic glutamic acid by hydrophobic valine at position 6 of the beta-subunit.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (2) 2027 bio.pdf, printed p. 8 (PDF p. 10)

explanations.explanation_text: Option C is the correct exam answer because it states a FALSE statement: polymerization and fibrous aggregation of HbS occur predominantly in the DEOXY-HbS (taut/unoxygenated) state, where hydrophobic sticky patches are exposed, NOT in the oxy-form.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (2) 2027 bio.pdf, printed p. 8 (PDF p. 10)

explanations.explanation_text: Homozygous inheritance of HbS causes classical sickle cell anemia with chronic hemolytic anemia and painful vaso-occlusive crises.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (2) 2027 bio.pdf, printed p. 8 (PDF p. 10)

explanations.explanation_text: Fluoroquinolones inhibit bacterial DNA gyrase (topoisomerase II) and topoisomerase IV, preventing DNA replication.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 48 (PDF p. 51)

explanations.explanation_text: Option B is the correct exam answer because fluoroquinolones are NOT active against spirochetes like Treponema pallidum (syphilis); penicillin G remains the drug of choice for Treponema pallidum.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed pp. 31, 49 (PDF pp. 34, 52)

explanations.explanation_text: Fluoroquinolones carry a well-known risk of tendinitis and tendon rupture (especially the Achilles tendon).
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 51 (PDF p. 54)

explanations.explanation_text: Fluoroquinolones possess broad-spectrum, concentration-dependent bactericidal activity against Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed pp. 48, 49 (PDF pp. 51, 52)

explanations.explanation_text: Plasmodium vivax is transmitted by female Anopheles mosquitoes, not Culex.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 34 (PDF p. 39)

explanations.explanation_text: Trypanosoma brucei is transmitted by tsetse flies of the genus Glossina, not mosquitoes.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 64 (PDF p. 69)

explanations.explanation_text: Leishmania donovani is biologically transmitted in the Old World by female sandflies of the genus Phlebotomus.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 77, 78 (PDF pp. 82, 83)

explanations.explanation_text: Wuchereria bancrofti is transmitted by mosquitoes (chiefly Culex pipiens in Egypt), while Ixodes ticks transmit Babesia and Borrelia.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 19, 50 (PDF pp. 24, 55)

explanations.explanation_text: Nephrotoxicity is characteristic of aminoglycosides, amphotericin B, and vancomycin, not chloramphenicol.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed pp. 36, 41, 52 (PDF pp. 39, 44, 55)

explanations.explanation_text: Ototoxicity is typical of aminoglycosides.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 41 (PDF p. 44)

explanations.explanation_text: Bone marrow depression is the most serious and clinically limiting adverse effect of chloramphenicol, manifesting as both a dose-dependent reversible erythroid suppression and an idiosyncratic, non-dose-dependent, fatal aplastic anemia.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed pp. 44, 45 (PDF pp. 47, 48)

explanations.explanation_text: Tendon rupture is caused by fluoroquinolones.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 51 (PDF p. 54)

explanations.explanation_text: In homozygous alpha-thalassemia (deletion of all 4 alpha-globin genes), the total absence of alpha chains leads to the accumulation of homotetramers of gamma chains (gamma4), known as Hemoglobin Bart’s, resulting in fatal hydrops fetalis.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (2) 2027 bio.pdf, printed p. 10 (PDF p. 12)

explanations.explanation_text: Thalassemia is an inherited autosomal recessive genetic disease caused by mutations or deletions in globin genes, not an acquired disorder.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (2) 2027 bio.pdf, printed pp. 9, 10 (PDF pp. 11, 12)

explanations.explanation_text: Thalassemia is characterized by microcytic hypochromic hemolytic anemia (low MCV < 80 fL), not macrocytic anemia.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 24 (PDF p. 27)

explanations.explanation_text: Thalassemias affect either alpha-globin chains (alpha-thalassemia) or beta-globin chains (beta-thalassemia).
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (2) 2027 bio.pdf, printed pp. 9, 10 (PDF pp. 11, 12)

explanations.explanation_text: In nodular lymphocyte predominant Hodgkin lymphoma (NLPHL), the diagnostic malignant cell is the L&H (lymphocytic and histiocytic) variant of the Reed-Sternberg cell, characteristically displaying a folded, multi-lobed "popcorn" nucleus.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (3) 2027 pathology.pdf, printed pp. 14, 16 (PDF pp. 15, 17)

explanations.explanation_text: Langhans giant cells are non-neoplastic multinucleated giant cells with horseshoe-arranged nuclei seen in tuberculous granulomas.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (3) 2027 pathology.pdf, printed pp. 5, 6 (PDF pp. 6, 7)

explanations.explanation_text: Epithelioid cells are activated, modified macrophages found in granulomatous inflammation.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (3) 2027 pathology.pdf, printed p. 5 (PDF p. 6)

explanations.explanation_text: Reactive small B and T lymphocytes form the non-neoplastic background cellular milieu, not the neoplastic clone.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (3) 2027 pathology.pdf, printed p. 16 (PDF p. 17)

explanations.explanation_text: Cervical lymph nodes are the most common site of metastatic carcinoma from primary malignancies of the head, neck, thyroid, lung, and upper gastrointestinal tract.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (3) 2027 pathology.pdf, printed pp. 3, 5 (PDF pp. 4, 6)

explanations.explanation_text: Extramedullary hematopoiesis occurs predominantly in the spleen and liver during severe marrow failure or myelofibrosis, rarely presenting primarily in cervical nodes.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (3) 2027 pathology.pdf, printed p. 18 (PDF p. 19)

explanations.explanation_text: Amyloid deposition is a systemic or organ-specific protein disorder, far less common in cervical nodes than metastatic neoplasia.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (3) 2027 pathology.pdf, printed p. 19 (PDF p. 20)

explanations.explanation_text: Penicillins cause hypersensitivity and interstitial nephritis (notably methicillin), but not Fanconi syndrome.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 33 (PDF p. 36)

explanations.explanation_text: Macrolides cause cholestatic hepatitis and gastrointestinal motility stimulation, not proximal renal tubular defects.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 42 (PDF p. 45)

explanations.explanation_text: Cephalosporins can cause tubular necrosis in high doses with aminoglycosides, not outdated Fanconi syndrome.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 34 (PDF p. 37)

explanations.explanation_text: Outdated or degraded tetracycline formulations decompose into toxic degradation products (epitetracycline and anhydrotetracycline) that cause toxic injury to the renal proximal tubules, presenting as Fanconi syndrome (aminoaciduria, glycosuria, phosphaturia, and metabolic acidosis).
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 39 (PDF p. 42)

explanations.explanation_text: Elevated CSF protein (>35 mg/dL) is a hallmark of Stage 2 (meningo-encephalitic) HAT.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 70 (PDF p. 75)

explanations.explanation_text: Demonstration of polymorphic trypomastigotes in centrifuged CSF is definitive for Stage 2 CNS involvement.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 67, 70 (PDF pp. 72, 75)

explanations.explanation_text: Option C is the correct exam answer because it states the FALSE finding: Stage 2 HAT is officially defined by a marked lymphocytic pleocytosis with CSF WBC count GREATER than 20 cells/uL (not < 20), together with elevated protein and Mott cells.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 67, 70 (PDF pp. 72, 75)

explanations.explanation_text: Severe disruption of the circadian sleep-wake cycle (daytime somnolence and nocturnal insomnia) is the defining clinical feature that gave the disease the name sleeping sickness.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 67 (PDF p. 72)

explanations.explanation_text: Fungal cell wall beta-(1,3)-D-glucan synthesis is inhibited by echinocandins (e.g. caspofungin), not griseofulvin.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 51 (PDF p. 54)

explanations.explanation_text: Griseofulvin enters susceptible fungal cells and binds to polymerizing tubulin proteins, disrupting the fungal mitotic spindle apparatus and arresting fungal cell division at metaphase.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 53 (PDF p. 56)

explanations.explanation_text: Inhibition of DNA gyrase is the mechanism of fluoroquinolones.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 48 (PDF p. 51)

explanations.explanation_text: Inhibition of folic acid synthesis is the mechanism of sulfonamides and trimethoprim.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 46 (PDF p. 49)

explanations.explanation_text: Acanthamoeba exists in only two stages: active trophozoite and resistant double-walled cyst; it lacks a flagellated stage completely.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 88, 94 (PDF pp. 93, 99)

explanations.explanation_text: Entamoeba histolytica is an intestinal rhizopod amoeba that has only trophozoite, precyst, and cyst stages, without any flagellate form.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 86 (PDF p. 91)

explanations.explanation_text: Naegleria fowleri is an amoeboflagellate whose life cycle includes a temporary, pear-shaped, biflagellated non-dividing form that arises when amoeboid trophozoites are exposed to changes in ionic concentration or distilled water (enflagellation test).
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 84, 86, 94 (PDF pp. 89, 91, 99)

explanations.explanation_text: Toxoplasma gondii forms include tachyzoites, bradyzoites in tissue cysts, and sporozoites within oocysts; it does not produce a free flagellated stage.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 54, 55 (PDF pp. 59, 60)

explanations.explanation_text: Inhibition of transpeptidation is the mechanism of beta-lactam antibiotics.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 30 (PDF p. 33)

explanations.explanation_text: Aminoglycosides bind to the 30S ribosomal subunit, causing misreading of the mRNA template (incorporation of incorrect amino acids into the nascent polypeptide chain) and interfering with initiation, resulting in nonfunctional and lethal bacterial proteins.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 40 (PDF p. 43)

explanations.explanation_text: Blocking DNA-dependent RNA polymerase is the mechanism of rifampin.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 28 (PDF p. 31)

explanations.explanation_text: Inhibiting DNA topoisomerase (DNA gyrase) is the mechanism of fluoroquinolones.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 48 (PDF p. 51)

explanations.explanation_text: Indirect (unconjugated) bilirubin is lipid-soluble and insoluble in aqueous solutions; direct (conjugated) bilirubin is water-soluble.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (2) 2027 bio.pdf, printed p. 15 (PDF p. 17)

explanations.explanation_text: Because it is water-insoluble and bound to albumin, indirect bilirubin cannot pass through the renal glomerular filtration barrier into urine.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (2) 2027 bio.pdf, printed p. 16 (PDF p. 18)

explanations.explanation_text: Indirect bilirubin formed by macrophages of the reticuloendothelial system is hydrophobic and is transported through the bloodstream to hepatocytes non-covalently bound to plasma albumin.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (2) 2027 bio.pdf, printed pp. 14, 15 (PDF pp. 16, 17)

explanations.explanation_text: Bilirubin conjugated with glucuronic acid (bilirubin diglucuronide) is direct, conjugated bilirubin.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (2) 2027 bio.pdf, printed pp. 14, 15 (PDF pp. 16, 17)

explanations.explanation_text: This statement is correct: abciximab is a chimeric Fab fragment that directly inhibits glycoprotein IIb/IIIa receptors.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed pp. 11, 12 (PDF pp. 14, 15)

explanations.explanation_text: This statement is correct: by preventing fibrinogen binding to GP IIb/IIIa receptors on adjacent platelets, it potently inhibits platelet aggregation.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed pp. 11, 12 (PDF pp. 14, 15)

explanations.explanation_text: Option C is designated as the INCORRECT statement (and thus the correct exam answer): abciximab is engineered as a chimeric monoclonal Fab fragment with humanized constant regions designed specifically to avoid immunogenicity and neutralization during clinical use.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 12 (PDF p. 15)

explanations.explanation_text: This statement is correct: abciximab is given by intravenous bolus followed by continuous IV infusion; it is not orally active.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 12 (PDF p. 15)

explanations.explanation_text: Ascaris lumbricoides is diagnosed by detecting characteristic bile-stained fertile or unfertile eggs in stool microscopy.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 103 (PDF p. 108)

explanations.explanation_text: Enterobius vermicularis is diagnosed by detecting planoconvex eggs on perianal skin using the cellophane tape (Scotch tape) technique.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 107 (PDF p. 112)

explanations.explanation_text: Serological testing for specific antibodies (IgM, IgG, IgA, IgE, Sabin-Feldman dye test, ELISA) is the mainstay and primary diagnostic modality for Toxoplasma gondii infection in clinical practice.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 60, 61 (PDF pp. 65, 66)

explanations.explanation_text: Trichuris trichiura is diagnosed directly by finding characteristic barrel-shaped eggs with bipolar mucus plugs in stool samples.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 101 (PDF p. 106)

explanations.explanation_text: Imipenem is not absorbed from the gastrointestinal tract and must be administered intravenously.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 35 (PDF p. 38)

explanations.explanation_text: Imipenem is excreted renally; elevated drug concentrations in renal impairment increase the risk of central nervous system toxicity and seizures, necessitating dosage reduction based on creatinine clearance.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 35 (PDF p. 38)

explanations.explanation_text: Imipenem is highly active against Gram-positive bacteria (including Streptococcus, Listeria, and methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus).
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 35 (PDF p. 38)

explanations.explanation_text: Imipenem penetrates well across inflamed meninges into the CSF.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (4) 2027-pharma.pdf, printed p. 35 (PDF p. 38)

explanations.explanation_text: Plasmodium transmission in mosquitoes involves both developmental transformation and numerical multiplication (cyclopropagative transmission).
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 38 (PDF p. 43)

explanations.explanation_text: Leishmania transmission in sandflies involves morphogenesis and massive asexual multiplication (cyclopropagative development).
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 78, 79 (PDF pp. 83, 84)

explanations.explanation_text: In lymphatic filariasis (Wuchereria bancrofti), the ingested microfilaria undergoes morphological transformation and moulting into an infective third-stage larva (L3) inside the mosquito vector WITHOUT multiplying in number, defining CYCLO-DEVELOPMENTAL transmission.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 20 (PDF p. 25)

explanations.explanation_text: Trypanosoma brucei and T. cruzi undergo cyclopropagative development in their insect vectors (developmental change with numerical binary fission).
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 66, 73 (PDF pp. 71, 78)

explanations.explanation_text: Bather’s itch is caused by cercariae of non-human avian and mammalian schistosomes.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 17 (PDF p. 22)

explanations.explanation_text: Option B is the correct exam answer because it is FALSE: bather’s itch is caused specifically by NON-HUMAN (avian/animal) cercariae, NOT human schistosome cercariae.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 17 (PDF p. 22)

explanations.explanation_text: Clinically, it presents as severe itching, urticarial wheals, macules, and papules at the sites of skin penetration.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 17 (PDF p. 22)

explanations.explanation_text: Human cercariae penetrate the skin and migrate systematically to mature into adult worms.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 17 (PDF p. 22)

explanations.explanation_text: Plasmodium vivax causes benign tertian malaria, which does not characteristically trigger the sudden fulminant intravascular hemolytic crisis unique to asplenic babesiosis.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 32, 53 (PDF pp. 37, 58)

explanations.explanation_text: The spleen plays an indispensable filtering and immunological role in clearing intraerythrocytic Babesia; in splenectomized individuals, Babesia microti causes severe, fulminant, life-threatening infection characterized by massive intravascular hemolysis, hemoglobinuria, DIC, renal failure, and high mortality.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 51, 53 (PDF pp. 56, 58)

explanations.explanation_text: Leishmania donovani replicates inside macrophages causing visceral leishmaniasis; massive splenomegaly is its primary sign rather than post-splenectomy fulminant crises.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 79 (PDF p. 84)

explanations.explanation_text: Trypanosoma brucei is an extracellular flagellate whose virulence is governed by VSG antigenic variation rather than splenic filtration of RBCs.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 69 (PDF p. 74)

explanations.explanation_text: In American trypanosomiasis (Chagas disease), Trypanosoma cruzi amastigotes invade glandular tissue including the thyroid gland, causing chronic thyroiditis and thyroid insufficiency.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 71, 75 (PDF pp. 76, 80)

explanations.explanation_text: Toxoplasma gondii localizes mainly in the brain, eye, skeletal muscle, and myocardium, not characteristically presenting with thyroiditis.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 57, 59 (PDF pp. 62, 64)

explanations.explanation_text: Leishmania tropica causes localized cutaneous leishmaniasis (oriental sore), with no visceral or thyroid invasion.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 77 (PDF p. 82)

explanations.explanation_text: Wuchereria bancrofti is restricted to the lymphatic channels of the lower extremities, scrotum, and retroperitoneum.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed pp. 18, 21 (PDF pp. 23, 26)

explanations.explanation_text: In Chagas disease (American trypanosomiasis), clinical specimens cultured on NNN (Novy-MacNeal-Nicolle) medium yield motile epimastigotes and trypomastigotes within 1 to 6 weeks, providing a recognized direct diagnostic method.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 75 (PDF p. 80)

explanations.explanation_text: Malaria parasites are obligate intracellular protozoa diagnosed by Giemsa-stained blood films or QBC, not cultured on mycological Sabouraud dextrose agar.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 45 (PDF p. 50)

explanations.explanation_text: Malaria parasites are obligate intracellular protozoa diagnosed by Giemsa-stained blood films or QBC, not cultured on mycological Sabouraud dextrose agar.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 62 (PDF p. 67)

explanations.explanation_text: Leishmania requires specialized NNN medium or Schneider’s drosophila medium; MacConkey agar is a selective medium for Gram-negative enteric bacteria.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (1) 2027 para.pdf, printed p. 81 (PDF p. 86)

explanations.explanation_text: Oxidation of the heme iron from the reduced ferrous (Fe2+) state to the oxidized ferric (Fe3+) state forms methemoglobin (Met-Hb / hematin), which CANNOT reversibly bind molecular oxygen, resulting in functional tissue hypoxia and cyanosis.
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (2) 2027 bio.pdf, printed p. 6 (PDF p. 8)

explanations.explanation_text: Ferric iron in methemoglobin cannot bind oxygen at all; binding firmly and irreversibly to oxygen is not the mechanism of methemoglobinemia (firm binding to remaining subunits occurs with carbon monoxide).
explanations.source_document: HAEM 202 part (2) 2027 bio.pdf, printed p. 6 (PDF p. 8)

explanations.explanation_text: Oxidative conversion does not increase red cell flexibility; instead, oxidative injury promotes Heinz body formation and reduced erythrocyte deformability.

explanations.explanation_text: In anaerobic glycolysis, 4 ATP are generated at substrate level (by phosphoglycerate kinase and pyruvate kinase) and 2 ATP are consumed in the preparatory phase (by hexokinase and PFK-1), yielding a net gain of exactly 2 ATP per glucose molecule. The 2 NADH produced are re-oxidized by lactate dehydrogenase to regenerate NAD+, so no ETC ATP is formed. Under aerobic conditions, re-oxidation of 2 cytosolic NADH by the ETC yields up to 5 ATP, but under anaerobic conditions NADH cannot be oxidized by mitochondria. Four ATP represents the gross substrate-level ATP generation before subtracting the 2 ATP invested in the activation reactions. Incorrect: Seven ATP represents the net energy yield of aerobic glycolysis (4 substrate ATP + 5 ETC ATP - 2 consumed ATP = 7 ATP).

explanations.explanation_text: In diabetes mellitus, impaired glucose utilization forces reliance on fatty acid oxidation (RQ ≈ 0.70), causing the RQ to decrease significantly below normal. During prolonged fasting and starvation, glycogen stores are depleted and tissue energy is derived primarily from fat combustion, lowering RQ toward 0.70. In acidosis, excess H+ stimulates hyperventilation, which blows off extra CO2 from the bicarbonate buffer pool. Because CO2 output exceeds metabolic O2 consumption, the ratio (VCO2 / VO2) rises, increasing RQ above 1.0. Incorrect: In alkalosis, respiratory drive is depressed, retaining CO2 in body fluids; with less CO2 exhaled relative to O2 utilized, the measured RQ decreases.

explanations.explanation_text: Dermatological findings in ariboflavinosis include seborrheic dermatitis affecting the nasolabial folds and scrotum.

explanations.explanation_text: Hemolysis is precipitated by oxidant drugs (e.g., primaquine, sulfonamides) that generate reactive oxygen species (ROS) in erythrocytes lacking NADPH; they do NOT cause 'production of NADH instead of NADPH'.

explanations.explanation_text: The fundamental defect is the inability of mature erythrocytes to generate NADPH to protect against oxidative damage.

explanations.explanation_text: The satiety center acts by tonically inhibiting the inherent chronic activity of the feeding center, rather than stimulating it.

explanations.explanation_text: Ketolysis occurs in the mitochondria of extrahepatic tissues (skeletal muscle, heart, brain, renal cortex).

explanations.explanation_text: Ketolysis is STIMULATED by insulin (which promotes glucose uptake providing oxaloacetate for acetyl-CoA oxidation) and INHIBITED by anti-insulin hormones, which promote ketogenesis over peripheral ketolysis.

explanations.explanation_text: The thiophorase reaction requires succinyl-CoA from the TCA cycle to activate acetoacetate to acetoacetyl-CoA.

explanations.explanation_text: The phosphate-ester bond in glucose 6-phosphate is a low-energy bond, releasing less than 7.3 kcal/mol (~3.3 kcal/mol) upon hydrolysis.

explanations.explanation_text: Glycosidic bonds connecting monosaccharides in carbohydrates are low-energy covalent bonds releasing < 7.3 kcal/mol.

explanations.explanation_text: Peptide bonds linking amino acids in proteins are low-energy bonds releasing < 7.3 kcal/mol upon hydrolysis.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 38 (PDF p. 40)

explanations.explanation_text: The enol-phosphate bond in 2-phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP) is a very high-energy phosphate bond that releases -14.8 kcal/mol upon hydrolysis (far exceeding the 7.3 kcal/mol threshold for high-energy bonds), which drives the substrate-level synthesis of ATP by pyruvate kinase.

explanations.explanation_text: Pyridoxal 5'-phosphate (PLP), derived from Vitamin B6, functions primarily as the essential coenzyme for transaminases (ALT, AST), amino acid decarboxylases, dehydratases, desulfhydrases, and transsulfuration enzymes in amino acid metabolism.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 19, 98 (PDF pp. 21, 100)

explanations.explanation_text: Blood coagulation factor carboxylation requires Vitamin K (hydroquinone), not PLP.

explanations.explanation_text: De novo purine synthesis requires PRPP, glutamine, glycine, aspartate, and folate derivatives (THF), not PLP.

explanations.explanation_text: The main end products of pyrimidine catabolism are beta-alanine and beta-aminoisobutyrate (highly water-soluble); uric acid is the end product of PURINE catabolism, while urea is derived from amino acid deamination in the urea cycle.

explanations.explanation_text: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II (CPSII) is the cytosolic rate-limiting key enzyme for the de novo synthesis of pyrimidines.

explanations.explanation_text: The pyrimidine salvage system uses specific nucleoside kinases (uridine kinase, thymidine kinase, deoxycytidine kinase) to phosphorylate pyrimidine nucleosides.

explanations.explanation_text: Urinary beta-aminoisobutyrate originates exclusively from thymine degradation in DNA, serving as an endogenous marker of DNA turnover in leukemias and post-radiotherapy.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 126 (PDF p. 128)

explanations.explanation_text: Epinephrine is an adrenal medullary hormone involved in metabolic stimulation and non-shivering thermogenesis, not the transmitter at eccrine sweat gland neuroeffector junctions.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 25

explanations.explanation_text: Norepinephrine is the classic sympathetic postganglionic transmitter for vascular smooth muscle, but eccrine sweat gland innervation is a cholinergic exception.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, pp. 23, 26

explanations.explanation_text: Sweating is an active evaporative heat-loss process under sympathetic nervous control mediated by sympathetic cholinergic fibers that release acetylcholine, which is blocked by atropine.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 23

explanations.explanation_text: Dopamine functions as a central neurotransmitter, not as the peripheral secretomotor transmitter of sweat glands.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 23

explanations.explanation_text: SDA is primarily attributed to the energetic cost of intermediary metabolic reactions in the liver associated with the assimilation, transformation, and storage of absorbed nutrients.

explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 49, 133 (PDF pp. 51, 135)

explanations.explanation_text: Complete oxidation of acetyl-CoA requires the citric acid cycle and functional mitochondrial respiratory chain, which cannot proceed without oxygen.

explanations.explanation_text: Fatty acid oxidation is strictly aerobic and requires mitochondrial oxygen delivery; muscles cannot oxidize fatty acids anaerobically.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 72, 133 (PDF pp. 74, 135)

explanations.explanation_text: Calcium released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum allosterically ACTIVATES glycogenolysis (via phosphorylase kinase), PDH, and the TCA cycle.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 46, 52, 133 (PDF pp. 48, 54, 135)

explanations.explanation_text: Nicotinic acid (niacin) is a direct derivative of the kynurenine pathway of tryptophan catabolism (via quinolinate).

explanations.explanation_text: Tryptophan catabolism generates formylkynurenine, which yields FORMYL-THF (H-C=O); METHENYL-THF (=CH-) is not the direct one-carbon adduct formed from tryptophan ring cleavage.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 21, 115, 116 (PDF pp. 23, 117, 118)

explanations.explanation_text: Serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine) is synthesized directly from tryptophan via BH4-dependent tryptophan hydroxylase and aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 116 (PDF p. 118)

explanations.explanation_text: Melatonin is formed directly from serotonin in the pineal gland by N-acetylation and O-methylation.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 116 (PDF p. 118)

explanations.explanation_text: Hypothyroidism reduces metabolic activity in nearly all tissues, characteristically lowering BMR.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 10

explanations.explanation_text: Undernutrition and starvation induce a hypometabolic state with decreased BMR to conserve dwindling caloric reserves.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 10

explanations.explanation_text: Malignancy (due to uncontrolled cellular proliferation and hypercatabolism) and polycythemia (due to expanded cellular turnover and hematopoiesis) pathologically increase metabolic rate and BMR.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 10

explanations.explanation_text: Hypopituitarism diminishes trophic hormones (TSH, ACTH, GH), leading to secondary adrenal and thyroid insufficiency that lowers BMR.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 10

explanations.explanation_text: Non-shivering (chemical) thermogenesis is an increase in metabolic heat production independent of muscle contraction, mediated by epinephrine and thyroid hormone stimulating fat metabolism and uncoupling protein activity.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 25

explanations.explanation_text: Shivering thermogenesis is mediated by somatic motor neurons causing rapid oscillating contractions of skeletal muscles (10-20/sec), whereas brown fat uncoupling is non-shivering thermogenesis.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 25

explanations.explanation_text: Endogenous pyrogens induce fever centrally by stimulating hypothalamic prostaglandin synthesis to elevate the set point, which triggers heat-gain mechanisms (vasoconstriction and shivering), not sweating.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 28

explanations.explanation_text: Cutaneous vasoconstriction reduces superficial blood flow, minimizing radiative and convective heat dissipation rather than promoting it.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 26

explanations.explanation_text: Peptide YY (PYY) is secreted by the intestines during and after meals, inhibiting appetite-stimulating NPY neurons to signal satiety and decrease food intake.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 15

explanations.explanation_text: Leptin binding to POMC neurons stimulates alpha-MSH, which reduces food intake and increases energy expenditure.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, pp. 12, 16

explanations.explanation_text: Distension of the stomach provides neural sensory input indicating fullness, activating the satiety center and terminating feeding.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, pp. 13, 15

explanations.explanation_text: Low glucose utilization in hypothalamic satiety center glucostats decreases their inhibitory output, thereby disinhibiting the feeding center and increasing appetite and food intake.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 14

explanations.explanation_text: Complete autoimmune destruction of beta-cells is the defining etiology of Type 1A DM, not Type 2 DM.

explanations.explanation_text: Type 2 DM is fundamentally characterized by insulin resistance on the background of obesity, which triggers compensatory hyperinsulinemia before eventual beta-cell decompensation.

explanations.explanation_text: IDE (insulin-degrading enzyme) genetic deficiency is not the primary cause of clinical Type 2 diabetes.

explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 104, 105 (PDF pp. 106, 107)

explanations.explanation_text: Valine is converted to succinyl-CoA and does not produce glyoxylate or oxalate.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 115 (PDF p. 117)

explanations.explanation_text: Tryptophan is degraded via the kynurenine pathway to form formyl-THF, alanine, and nicotinic acid; it does not yield oxalate.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 107 (PDF p. 109)

explanations.explanation_text: Glycine is deaminated by glycine oxidase to form glyoxylic acid; genetic failure of glyoxylate transamination or oxidation causes glyoxylate to be converted by lactate dehydrogenase into oxalate, precipitating as calcium oxalate crystals in urine (hyperoxaluria and nephrocalcinosis).
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 107 (PDF p. 109)

explanations.explanation_text: IDE (insulin-degrading enzyme) genetic deficiency is not the primary cause of clinical Type 2 diabetes.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 90 (PDF p. 92)

explanations.explanation_text: Complete autoimmune destruction of beta-cells is the defining etiology of Type 1A DM, not Type 2 DM.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 93 (PDF p. 95)

explanations.explanation_text: Type 2 DM is fundamentally characterized by insulin resistance on the background of obesity, which triggers compensatory hyperinsulinemia before eventual beta-cell decompensation.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 91, 93 (PDF pp. 93, 95)

explanations.explanation_text: Overproduction of lung surfactant is unrelated to diabetes mellitus (deficiency causes neonatal RDS).
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 85 (PDF p. 87)

explanations.explanation_text: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS) in premature infants is caused by a developmental deficiency of pulmonary lung surfactant (dipalmitoyl lecithin / phosphatidylcholine), resulting in alveolar collapse and respiratory failure.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 85 (PDF p. 87)

explanations.explanation_text: Increased IgG and phospholipids in cerebrospinal fluid is a diagnostic feature of multiple sclerosis, not RDS.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 85 (PDF p. 87)

explanations.explanation_text: Accumulation of glucosyl ceramide in tissues occurs in Gaucher's disease due to beta-glucosidase deficiency.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 85 (PDF p. 87)

explanations.explanation_text: Demyelination of central white matter characterizes multiple sclerosis, not infant RDS.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 85 (PDF p. 87)

explanations.explanation_text: Nicotinic acid (niacin) is a direct derivative of the kynurenine pathway of tryptophan catabolism (via quinolinate).
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 116 (PDF p. 118)

explanations.explanation_text: Orexins are produced by the lateral hypothalamic area (feeding center) to stimulate food intake, not by the ventromedial nuclei.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 13

explanations.explanation_text: Destruction of the ventromedial satiety center causes loss of inhibition over the feeding center, leading to hyperphagia and obesity, not fatal anorexia.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 11

explanations.explanation_text: The satiety center acts by tonically inhibiting the inherent chronic activity of the feeding center, rather than stimulating it.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 14

explanations.explanation_text: Unlike most brain regions which take up glucose independently of insulin, glucostat neurons in the ventromedial satiety center depend on insulin for glucose utilization.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 13

explanations.explanation_text: Evaporative heat loss occurs continually at all environmental temperatures, even in freezing cold, via insensible perspiration from the skin and continuous water loss from respiratory mucous membranes, dissipating 0.6 kcal per cc of evaporated water.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 23

explanations.explanation_text: Radiation depends on a thermal gradient between the body surface and surrounding objects; when ambient temperature exceeds skin temperature, the body absorbs radiant heat rather than losing it.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 22

explanations.explanation_text: Conduction requires a direct thermal gradient down which heat can flow to cooler contacting objects or air; if the environment is warmer than the skin, heat is conducted into the body.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 22

explanations.explanation_text: Convection dissipates heat only when cooler air replaces warmed air around the body; if ambient air currents are hotter than skin temperature, convection transfers heat into the body.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 23

explanations.explanation_text: The pyrimidine salvage system uses specific nucleoside kinases (uridine kinase, thymidine kinase, deoxycytidine kinase) to phosphorylate pyrimidine nucleosides.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 101, 122, 126 (PDF pp. 103, 124, 128)

explanations.explanation_text: The main end products of pyrimidine catabolism are beta-alanine and beta-aminoisobutyrate (highly water-soluble); uric acid is the end product of PURINE catabolism, while urea is derived from amino acid deamination in the urea cycle.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 125, 126 (PDF pp. 127, 128)

explanations.explanation_text: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II (CPSII) is the cytosolic rate-limiting key enzyme for the de novo synthesis of pyrimidines.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 125 (PDF p. 127)

explanations.explanation_text: Urinary beta-aminoisobutyrate originates exclusively from thymine degradation in DNA, serving as an endogenous marker of DNA turnover in leukemias and post-radiotherapy.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 126 (PDF p. 128)

explanations.explanation_text: Dermatological findings in ariboflavinosis include seborrheic dermatitis affecting the nasolabial folds and scrotum.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 17 (PDF p. 19)

explanations.explanation_text: Riboflavin deficiency characteristically causes angular stomatitis (painful fissures and inflammation at the angles of the mouth).
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 17 (PDF p. 19)

explanations.explanation_text: Riboflavin deficiency does not cause microcytic anemia; microcytic hypochromic anemia is caused by iron deficiency or Vitamin B6 deficiency (impaired ALA synthase in heme synthesis).
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 17 (PDF p. 19)

explanations.explanation_text: Ocular manifestations of riboflavin deficiency include circumcorneal conjunctival injection and vascularization of the cornea.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 19, 25 (PDF pp. 21, 27)

explanations.explanation_text: Serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine) is synthesized directly from tryptophan via BH4-dependent tryptophan hydroxylase and aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 18, 115 (PDF pp. 20, 117)

explanations.explanation_text: Melatonin is formed directly from serotonin in the pineal gland by N-acetylation and O-methylation.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 21, 115, 116 (PDF pp. 23, 117, 118)

explanations.explanation_text: Tryptophan catabolism generates formylkynurenine, which yields FORMYL-THF (H-C=O); METHENYL-THF (=CH-) is not the direct one-carbon adduct formed from tryptophan ring cleavage.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 116 (PDF p. 118)

explanations.explanation_text: Heat stroke happens upon exposure to high temperatures especially in humid air (up to 100% humidified), where high atmospheric water saturation prevents evaporative heat loss.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 28

explanations.explanation_text: Heat stroke happens upon exposure to high temperatures especially in humid air (up to 100% humidified), where high atmospheric water saturation prevents evaporative heat loss.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, pp. 25, 28

explanations.explanation_text: Heat stroke is caused by a failure and depression of hypothalamic heat-regulating ability when the brain becomes excessively heated.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, pp. 23, 28

explanations.explanation_text: Heat stroke is characterized by extreme hyperthermia, hot skin, and depressed thermoregulation, whereas shivering is a response to cold.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 28

explanations.explanation_text: During starvation, the body shifts from carbohydrate utilization to burning endogenous triglycerides; the catabolism of fats requires extra oxygen to oxidize hydrogen atoms, reducing CO2 output relative to O2 uptake and dropping the RQ to approximately 0.70.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 7

explanations.explanation_text: Violent muscular exercise causes lactic acidosis and hyperventilation, washing out CO2 and driving RQ well above 1.0.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 7

explanations.explanation_text: Violent muscular exercise causes lactic acidosis and hyperventilation, washing out CO2 and driving RQ well above 1.0.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, pp. 6, 7

explanations.explanation_text: When carbohydrates are converted into fats, an oxygen-rich compound is transformed into an oxygen-poor compound, releasing internal oxygen and reducing external O2 demand, which increases RQ above 1.0.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, pp. 6, 7

explanations.explanation_text: Peptide YY (PYY) is secreted by the intestines during and after meals, inhibiting appetite-stimulating NPY neurons to signal satiety and decrease food intake.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 15

explanations.explanation_text: Low glucose utilization in hypothalamic satiety center glucostats decreases their inhibitory output, thereby disinhibiting the feeding center and increasing appetite and food intake.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, pp. 12, 16

explanations.explanation_text: Leptin binding to POMC neurons stimulates alpha-MSH, which reduces food intake and increases energy expenditure.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, pp. 13, 15

explanations.explanation_text: Distension of the stomach provides neural sensory input indicating fullness, activating the satiety center and terminating feeding.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 14

explanations.explanation_text: The fundamental defect is the inability of mature erythrocytes to generate NADPH to protect against oxidative damage.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 59 (PDF p. 61)

explanations.explanation_text: G6PD deficiency impairs the generation of NADPH, preventing the regeneration of reduced glutathione (GSH) needed to detoxify H2O2.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 59 (PDF p. 61)

explanations.explanation_text: Hemolysis is precipitated by oxidant drugs (e.g., primaquine, sulfonamides) that generate reactive oxygen species (ROS) in erythrocytes lacking NADPH; they do NOT cause 'production of NADH instead of NADPH'.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 59 (PDF p. 61)

explanations.explanation_text: Ingestion of fava beans containing divicine and convicine triggers acute lipid peroxidation of red cell membranes, hemolysis, and jaundice.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 59 (PDF p. 61)

explanations.explanation_text: Fatty acid oxidation is strictly aerobic and requires mitochondrial oxygen delivery; muscles cannot oxidize fatty acids anaerobically.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 49, 133 (PDF pp. 51, 135)

explanations.explanation_text: Calcium released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum allosterically ACTIVATES glycogenolysis (via phosphorylase kinase), PDH, and the TCA cycle.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 42, 46 (PDF pp. 44, 48)

explanations.explanation_text: Complete oxidation of acetyl-CoA requires the citric acid cycle and functional mitochondrial respiratory chain, which cannot proceed without oxygen.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 72, 133 (PDF pp. 74, 135)

explanations.explanation_text: During anaerobic exercise, contracted muscle fibers compress intramyocellular microvessels, creating tissue hypoxia; the muscle relies on glycogenolysis followed by anaerobic glycolysis to convert pyruvate into lactic acid via lactate dehydrogenase.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 46, 52, 133 (PDF pp. 48, 54, 135)

explanations.explanation_text: Ketolysis is STIMULATED by insulin (which promotes glucose uptake providing oxaloacetate for acetyl-CoA oxidation) and INHIBITED by anti-insulin hormones, which promote ketogenesis over peripheral ketolysis.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 87 (PDF p. 89)

explanations.explanation_text: The thiophorase reaction requires succinyl-CoA from the TCA cycle to activate acetoacetate to acetoacetyl-CoA.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 87 (PDF p. 89)

explanations.explanation_text: Ketolysis occurs in the mitochondria of extrahepatic tissues (skeletal muscle, heart, brain, renal cortex).
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 87 (PDF p. 89)

explanations.explanation_text: Ketolysis is the complete metabolic oxidation of acetoacetate and beta-hydroxybutyrate to CO2 and H2O.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 87 (PDF p. 89)

explanations.explanation_text: Blood coagulation factor carboxylation requires Vitamin K (hydroquinone), not PLP.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 4 (PDF p. 6)

explanations.explanation_text: De novo purine synthesis requires PRPP, glutamine, glycine, aspartate, and folate derivatives (THF), not PLP.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 19, 98 (PDF pp. 21, 100)

explanations.explanation_text: Carbohydrate digestion in the GI tract is mediated by amylases and disaccharidases, which do not utilize PLP coenzymes.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 14 (PDF p. 16)

explanations.explanation_text: Pyridoxal 5'-phosphate (PLP), derived from Vitamin B6, functions primarily as the essential coenzyme for transaminases (ALT, AST), amino acid decarboxylases, dehydratases, desulfhydrases, and transsulfuration enzymes in amino acid metabolism.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 120 (PDF p. 122)

explanations.explanation_text: Conversion of malate to oxaloacetate is catalyzed by malate dehydrogenase; pyruvate does not directly react with malate dehydrogenase.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 52, 53 (PDF pp. 54, 55)

explanations.explanation_text: Triokinase phosphorylates D-glyceraldehyde to glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate in fructose metabolism; it does not convert pyruvate to glycerol-3-phosphate.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 49, 52 (PDF pp. 51, 54)

explanations.explanation_text: Under anaerobic conditions, pyruvate is reduced to L-lactate by lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), regenerating cytosolic NAD+ to sustain glycolysis.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 43, 53 (PDF pp. 45, 55)

explanations.explanation_text: Pyruvate carboxylase converts pyruvate into oxaloacetate (consuming ATP and CO2); conversion of pyruvate to active acetate (acetyl-CoA) is catalyzed by pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH).
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 65 (PDF p. 67)

explanations.explanation_text: Dopamine functions as a central neurotransmitter, not as the peripheral secretomotor transmitter of sweat glands.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 25

explanations.explanation_text: Sweating is an active evaporative heat-loss process under sympathetic nervous control mediated by sympathetic cholinergic fibers that release acetylcholine, which is blocked by atropine.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, pp. 23, 26

explanations.explanation_text: Norepinephrine is the classic sympathetic postganglionic transmitter for vascular smooth muscle, but eccrine sweat gland innervation is a cholinergic exception.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 23

explanations.explanation_text: Epinephrine is an adrenal medullary hormone involved in metabolic stimulation and non-shivering thermogenesis, not the transmitter at eccrine sweat gland neuroeffector junctions.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 23

explanations.explanation_text: Hypothyroidism reduces metabolic activity in nearly all tissues, characteristically lowering BMR.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 10

explanations.explanation_text: Malignancy (due to uncontrolled cellular proliferation and hypercatabolism) and polycythemia (due to expanded cellular turnover and hematopoiesis) pathologically increase metabolic rate and BMR.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 10

explanations.explanation_text: Hypopituitarism diminishes trophic hormones (TSH, ACTH, GH), leading to secondary adrenal and thyroid insufficiency that lowers BMR.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 10

explanations.explanation_text: Undernutrition and starvation induce a hypometabolic state with decreased BMR to conserve dwindling caloric reserves.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 10

explanations.explanation_text: Vitamin E (alpha-tocopherol) donates a phenolic hydrogen atom to neutralize lipid peroxyl radicals (LOO•), functioning as the primary chain-breaking antioxidant in lipid membranes.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 13 (PDF p. 15)

explanations.explanation_text: Premature infants have low adipose reserves and impaired placental transfer of Vitamin E, making erythrocyte membranes susceptible to oxidative damage and hemolytic anemia.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 13 (PDF p. 15)

explanations.explanation_text: Vitamin E specifically intercepts free radicals to protect polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) in cell membrane phospholipids from oxidative lipid peroxidation.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 14 (PDF p. 16)

explanations.explanation_text: Activation of hepatic clotting factors II, VII, IX, and X by gamma-carboxylation is the specific function of Vitamin K, not Vitamin E.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 13 (PDF p. 15)

explanations.explanation_text: Increased intraocular pressure is the defining pathological mechanism of glaucoma, not Vitamin A deficiency.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 12 (PDF p. 14)

explanations.explanation_text: In Vitamin A deficiency, loss of retinoic acid-dependent epithelial maintenance leads to squamous metaplasia and atrophy of the lacrimal gland and conjunctival goblet cells, halting tear secretion and producing dry eye (xerophthalmia) and corneal ulceration.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 12 (PDF p. 14)

explanations.explanation_text: Optic nerve injury results from ischemia, traumatic compression, or toxic neuropathies, not primary Vitamin A deficiency.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 12 (PDF p. 14)

explanations.explanation_text: Corneal dryness (xerosis) and subsequent ulceration occur due to absent lubrication and keratinization, whereas corneal edema results from endothelial failure or acute fluid retention.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 12 (PDF p. 14)

explanations.explanation_text: SDA is dependent on the type of macronutrient (proteins produce 30% vs carbohydrates/fats 4-6%), but it is directly proportional to the quantity of food rather than the 'type' in a linear mathematical sense.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 9

explanations.explanation_text: SDA is defined as a temporary, postprandial increase in metabolic rate above basal levels that occurs after food consumption and subsides once metabolic processing is complete.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 9

explanations.explanation_text: Sweating is an active evaporative process extruded by eccrine glands under sympathetic cholinergic control, not a passive process.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 23

explanations.explanation_text: Shivering is a mechanism for heat production during acute cold exposure, not during prolonged heat exposure (which causes anti-rise measures).
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, pp. 25, 27

explanations.explanation_text: Core body temperature normally exhibits a circadian (diurnal) fluctuation of approximately 1°C over a 24-hour cycle, reaching its lowest point in the early morning and its peak in the late afternoon.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 20

explanations.explanation_text: Radiation accounts for approximately 60% of total heat loss from the body in comfortable surroundings, not 15% (conduction and convection account for 15%).
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, pp. 22, 23

explanations.explanation_text: To compensate for peripheral insulin resistance in skeletal muscle and liver, pancreatic beta-cells increase insulin secretion, leading to compensatory hyperinsulinemia (fasting insulin > 25 microU/mL), a cardinal biomarker of metabolic syndrome.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 91, 92 (PDF pp. 93, 94)

explanations.explanation_text: Insulin resistance is associated with impaired fasting glucose and hyperglycemia due to unchecked hepatic gluconeogenesis, not hypoglycemia.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 91, 92 (PDF pp. 93, 94)

explanations.explanation_text: Hepatic VLDL synthesis and plasma triglycerides are increased (dyslipidemia) rather than decreased in insulin resistance and metabolic syndrome.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 36, 92 (PDF pp. 38, 94)

explanations.explanation_text: Insulin resistance is characterized by decreased GLUT-4 translocation and diminished glucose uptake in skeletal muscle, rather than an increase.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 91 (PDF p. 93)

explanations.explanation_text: Insulin decreases as portal glucose declines; insulin and glucagon move in opposite reciprocal directions.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 129 (PDF p. 131)

explanations.explanation_text: Glucagon secretion increases (not decreases) as blood glucose falls between meals.

explanations.explanation_text: Heme synthesis requires succinyl-CoA and glycine (catalyzed by ALA synthase), and does not incorporate free metabolic CO2.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 21, 44 (PDF pp. 23, 46)

explanations.explanation_text: Pyruvate is synthesized from glucose via glycolysis or from alanine via transamination; it is not formed by carboxylation reactions.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 49, 98 (PDF pp. 51, 100)

explanations.explanation_text: Propionyl-CoA is formed during beta-oxidation of odd-chain fatty acids or catabolism of isoleucine, valine, methionine, and threonine; it consumes CO2 to form methylmalonyl-CoA.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 45, 74, 107 (PDF pp. 47, 76, 109)

explanations.explanation_text: CO2 produced by oxidative decarboxylations in the Krebs cycle is utilized as a one-carbon donor to form Carbon-6 (C6) of the purine ring during de novo purine nucleotide synthesis.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 45, 120 (PDF pp. 47, 122)

explanations.explanation_text: Thiophorase (succinyl-CoA:acetoacetate-CoA transferase) is strictly an enzyme of ketolysis (ketone body oxidation) present in extrahepatic tissues and absent in liver.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 87 (PDF p. 89)

explanations.explanation_text: Ketogenesis occurs in the mitochondrial matrix of liver cells and specifically requires mitochondrial HMG-CoA synthase and HMG-CoA lyase to generate acetoacetate.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 86 (PDF p. 88)

explanations.explanation_text: Acetyl-CoA carboxylase is the key regulatory enzyme of fatty acid synthesis in the cytoplasm.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 77 (PDF p. 79)

explanations.explanation_text: Pyruvate carboxylase is an anaplerotic enzyme converting pyruvate to oxaloacetate in gluconeogenesis.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 53 (PDF p. 55)

explanations.explanation_text: Glycogen phosphorylase is the key regulatory enzyme of glycogenolysis (glycogen breakdown), not glycogenesis.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 62 (PDF p. 64)

explanations.explanation_text: Glucokinase phosphorylates free glucose to glucose 6-phosphate in the liver, initiating general carbohydrate metabolism.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 51 (PDF p. 53)

explanations.explanation_text: Glycogen synthase is the key, rate-limiting regulatory enzyme of glycogenesis, transferring glucosyl units from UDP-glucose to elongate glycogen branches via alpha-1,4-glucosidic bonds.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 61 (PDF p. 63)

explanations.explanation_text: Phosphofructokinase-1 (PFK-1) is the rate-limiting enzyme of glycolysis.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 50 (PDF p. 52)

explanations.explanation_text: Secondary active transport of glucose and galactose across the apical enterocyte brush-border membrane by SGLT-1 couples glucose influx to the downhill sodium electrochemical gradient; inhibition or deficiency of the basolateral Na+/K+-ATPase halts active Na+ extrusion, collapsing the gradient and completely arresting the active transport of glucose against its concentration gradient.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 5, 47 (PDF pp. 7, 49)

explanations.explanation_text: Fructose absorption across the apical membrane occurs via facilitated diffusion via GLUT-5, which is a sodium-independent passive uniporter unaffected by the Na+/K+-ATPase pump.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 5, 47 (PDF pp. 7, 49)

explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 5, 47 (PDF pp. 7, 49)

explanations.explanation_text: Passive diffusion of pentoses down concentration gradients does not require metabolic energy, carrier proteins, or electrochemical sodium gradients.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 5, 47 (PDF pp. 7, 49)

explanations.explanation_text: Antimycin A inhibits Complex III (cytochrome b-c1 complex), which blocks electron transfer from ubiquinone (CoQ) to cytochrome c, arresting electron transfer from BOTH NADH and FADH2.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 42 (PDF p. 44)

explanations.explanation_text: Cyanide binds to the heme Fe3+ in Complex IV (cytochrome c oxidase), completely shutting down the terminal reduction of O2 and arresting both NADH and FADH2 pathways.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 42 (PDF p. 44)

explanations.explanation_text: Oligomycin binds to the F0 subunit of ATP synthase (Complex V), inhibiting proton translocation and halting ATP synthesis without selectively targeting NADH transfer.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 42 (PDF p. 44)

explanations.explanation_text: Rotenone is a specific inhibitor of Complex I (NADH dehydrogenase complex) that prevents electron transfer from iron-sulfur centers of Complex I to ubiquinone (CoQ); since FADH2 donates its electrons directly to CoQ via Complex II (succinate dehydrogenase), FADH2 oxidation remains completely unaffected.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 42 (PDF p. 44)

explanations.explanation_text: Hypoglycemic coma can occur in any patient with diabetes mellitus (Type 1 or Type 2) as an iatrogenic acute complication resulting from overtreatment (excessive insulin or sulfonylurea dose, delayed/missed meal, or strenuous unaccustomed physical exercise).
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 94, 95 (PDF pp. 96, 97)

explanations.explanation_text: Hypoglycemic coma develops rapidly within minutes to a few hours, unlike Hyperglycemic Hyperosmolar State (HHS) which develops insidiously over days to weeks.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 95 (PDF p. 97)

explanations.explanation_text: Serum osmolality is normal in hypoglycemia; marked hyperosmolality (> 320 mOsm/kg) is the hallmark of HHS.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 95 (PDF p. 97)

explanations.explanation_text: Fluid deficit is minimal in hypoglycemia, whereas severe dehydration (8–10 liters fluid deficit) occurs in HHS and 3–6 liters in DKA.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 95 (PDF p. 97)

explanations.explanation_text: Accumulation of galactose-1-phosphate occurs in classic galactosemia due to GALT deficiency, not favism.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 66 (PDF p. 68)

explanations.explanation_text: Hemolytic anemia in favism is caused by an X-linked genetic deficiency of G6PD, the first rate-limiting enzyme of the Pentose Phosphate Pathway (HMP shunt), which is the sole source of NADPH in red blood cells.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 59 (PDF p. 61)

explanations.explanation_text: Depletion of hepatic ATP occurs in hereditary fructose intolerance due to trapping of inorganic phosphate by fructose-1-phosphate.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 65, 66 (PDF pp. 67, 68)

explanations.explanation_text: Failure to reabsorb amino acids by renal tubules characterizes cystinuria or Hartnup disease, not favism.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 112, 117 (PDF pp. 114, 119)

explanations.explanation_text: A high carbohydrate diet stimulates insulin release, which suppresses lipolysis and ketogenesis.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 80, 88 (PDF pp. 82, 90)

explanations.explanation_text: Overproduction of insulin inhibits hormone-sensitive lipase and prevents the generation of free fatty acid substrates for ketogenesis.

explanations.explanation_text: Decreased mobilization of free fatty acids would starve the liver of substrates for beta-oxidation, halting ketogenesis.

explanations.explanation_text: Hormone-sensitive lipase (HSL) is the key, rate-limiting regulatory enzyme of lipolysis in adipose tissue, hydrolyzing stored intracellular triacylglycerol into diacylglycerol and free fatty acids.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 77 (PDF p. 79)

explanations.explanation_text: Lipoprotein lipase (LPL) hydrolyzes circulating extracellular triglycerides in chylomicrons and VLDL at the capillary endothelium, not intracellular adipocyte stores.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 80 (PDF p. 82)

explanations.explanation_text: Pancreatic lipase hydrolyzes dietary triglycerides in the small intestinal lumen during digestion.

explanations.explanation_text: Pyrogens act on the hypothalamus to elevate the thermoregulatory set point via prostaglandin production, initiating physiologic heat-conserving and heat-generating responses that cause fever.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, pp. 27, 28

explanations.explanation_text: Sweat evaporation is severely impaired in high environmental humidity, as ambient water vapor saturation blocks liquid vaporization from skin.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, pp. 23, 28

explanations.explanation_text: The anterior hypothalamus coordinates vasodilation and sweating (heat loss), whereas the posterior hypothalamus coordinates vasoconstriction and shivering.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, pp. 24, 27

explanations.explanation_text: Aspirin is an anti-inflammatory antipyretic that inhibits cyclooxygenase, decreasing prostaglandin production.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 28; Bio printed p. 84 (PDF p. 86)

explanations.explanation_text: Singulair is a leukotriene receptor antagonist; aspirin does not block leukotriene receptors.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 84 (PDF p. 86)

explanations.explanation_text: Phospholipase A2 is inhibited by steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (corticosteroids like hydrocortisone and prednisone), not aspirin.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 84 (PDF p. 86)

explanations.explanation_text: Aspirin exerts its anti-inflammatory, antipyretic, and analgesic actions by irreversibly inhibiting the cyclooxygenase (COX) enzyme via covalent serine acetylation, thereby shutting down the biosynthesis of pro-inflammatory prostaglandins.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 84 (PDF p. 86)

explanations.explanation_text: Aspirin does not activate adenylyl cyclase; it targets prostaglandin H synthase.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 84 (PDF p. 86)

explanations.explanation_text: Methotrexate and aminopterin competitively inhibit dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR); sulfonamides target an earlier bacterial enzyme.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 22 (PDF p. 24)

explanations.explanation_text: Sulfonamides are structural analogs of para-aminobenzoic acid (PABA) and act as competitive inhibitors of bacterial dihydropteroate synthase, which incorporates PABA into pteroic acid during folate synthesis.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 22 (PDF p. 24)

explanations.explanation_text: Inhibition of vitamin K epoxide reductase (VKOR) to prevent regeneration of hydroquinone is the mechanism of action of anticoagulants like warfarin, not sulfonamides.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 15 (PDF p. 17)

explanations.explanation_text: Uncoupling oxidative phosphorylation is the mechanism of uncouplers such as 2,4-dinitrophenol and thermogenin, not sulfonamides.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 42 (PDF p. 44)

explanations.explanation_text: Type 2 orotic aciduria is caused by an isolated genetic deficiency of orotidylate decarboxylase (the second domain of the bifunctional enzyme UMP synthase), whereas Type 1 orotic aciduria involves deficiencies of both orotate phosphoribosyltransferase and orotidylate decarboxylase.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 125 (PDF p. 127)
