explanations.explanation_text: Dihydroorotase catalyzes the cyclization of carbamoyl aspartate to dihydroorotate earlier in the de novo pathway.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 125 (PDF p. 127)

explanations.explanation_text: CPSII deficiency blocks the initial entry step, preventing the formation of carbamoyl phosphate and orotate entirely.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 125 (PDF p. 127)

explanations.explanation_text: Pyruvate kinase is regulated allosterically by fructose 1,6-bisphosphate and ATP, but is not a target of lipoate-binding arsenic poisoning.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 51 (PDF p. 53)

explanations.explanation_text: Citrate synthase is inhibited by ATP, NADH, and succinyl-CoA, but not directly by arsenic.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 45 (PDF p. 47)

explanations.explanation_text: Isocitrate dehydrogenase is regulated by ATP/ADP and NADH/NAD+ ratios, but lacks a lipoic acid catalytic arm.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 45 (PDF p. 47)

explanations.explanation_text: Arsenic compounds form a stable covalent complex with the essential thiol (-SH) groups of lipoic acid, inactivating the dihydrolipoyl transsuccinylase core of alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase and blocking the citric acid cycle.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 46 (PDF p. 48)

explanations.explanation_text: Decreased apolipoprotein synthesis is the primary cause of fatty liver in protein-energy malnutrition (kwashiorkor), whereas starvation is primarily driven by lipolysis.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 30, 36 (PDF pp. 32, 38)

explanations.explanation_text: During prolonged starvation, high glucagon and epinephrine stimulate hormone-sensitive lipase in adipose tissue, flooding the liver with massive quantities of mobilized free fatty acids (FFAs) that exceed the hepatic capacity for beta-oxidation, leading to re-esterification and hepatic triglyceride accumulation.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 36 (PDF p. 38)

explanations.explanation_text: Hepatic de novo lipogenesis is completely suppressed during starvation due to low insulin and inactivation of acetyl-CoA carboxylase.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 78, 131 (PDF pp. 80, 133)

explanations.explanation_text: Lipotoxicity from ceramides contributes to inflammatory ballooning in steatohepatitis (MASH), but is not the primary physiological initiating mechanism of lipid pooling during starvation.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 36 (PDF p. 38)

explanations.explanation_text: Phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency causes phenylketonuria (PKU).
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 113 (PDF p. 115)

explanations.explanation_text: Homogentisate oxidase deficiency causes alkaptonuria.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 115 (PDF p. 117)

explanations.explanation_text: Maple syrup urine disease is due to genetic deficiency of the mitochondrial branched-chain alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase complex.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 107 (PDF p. 109)

explanations.explanation_text: Cystathionine synthase deficiency causes classical homocystinuria.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 111 (PDF p. 113)

explanations.explanation_text: Kidneys excrete urea into urine but cannot synthesize urea de novo because they lack arginase.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 101, 102 (PDF pp. 103, 104)

explanations.explanation_text: Urea formation occurs exclusively in the liver because hepatocytes are the only cells that express the complete set of urea cycle enzymes, specifically arginase, which hydrolyzes arginine to urea and ornithine.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 101 (PDF p. 103)

explanations.explanation_text: Brain tissue lacks a functional urea cycle and detoxifies ammonia by converting glutamate to glutamine.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 100, 102 (PDF pp. 102, 104)

explanations.explanation_text: Skeletal muscle exports excess amino acid nitrogen as alanine and glutamine to the liver for urea synthesis.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 55, 100 (PDF pp. 57, 102)

explanations.explanation_text: In primary hyperoxaluria, excessive hepatic oxalate production leads to heavy renal oxalate excretion; calcium oxalate has very poor urinary solubility, precipitating as recurrent bilateral nephrolithiasis and extensive tubular nephrocalcinosis, making the kidney the most severely damaged organ.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 105 (PDF p. 107)

explanations.explanation_text: The liver is the enzymatic site of glyoxylate synthesis, but oxalate precipitates and damages the renal parenchymal filtration and collecting system.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 105 (PDF p. 107)

explanations.explanation_text: The pancreas is not a primary target of calcium oxalate crystal deposition.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 105 (PDF p. 107)

explanations.explanation_text: The gallbladder forms cholesterol or bilirubin pigment stones, whereas hyperoxaluria specifically targets the urinary tract.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 105 (PDF p. 107)

explanations.explanation_text: Transaminases are large proteins (~100 kDa) that cannot pass the glomerular filtration barrier and are not excreted in urine.

explanations.explanation_text: Transaminases are not digestive enzymes and are not secreted into bile.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 119 (PDF p. 121)

explanations.explanation_text: ALT and AST are intracellular enzymes functioning in the cytosol and mitochondria; they appear in low baseline concentrations in normal plasma solely due to physiological cellular turnover, and surge into circulation only following acute tissue or hepatocellular damage.

explanations.explanation_text: Leptin is an appetite suppressor (anorexigenic hormone) that acts on the hypothalamus to decrease food intake and increase energy expenditure.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, pp. 15, 16

explanations.explanation_text: PYY acts by inhibiting NPY-secreting neurons in the arcuate nucleus, signaling satiety.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 15

explanations.explanation_text: Cholecystokinin (CCK) promotes the sense of fullness and satiety following meal ingestion, inhibiting the feeding center.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 15

explanations.explanation_text: Ghrelin, secreted primarily by the stomach fundus, is a potent hunger stimulant that surges before meals and activates appetite-stimulating NPY neurons in the hypothalamus.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 15

explanations.explanation_text: Glucokinase is the high-Km hepatic and pancreatic hexokinase isoform; red blood cells express Hexokinase-I.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 51 (PDF p. 53)

explanations.explanation_text: The inner mitochondrial membrane is impermeable to NADH; the primary function of the malate shuttle is to transfer reducing equivalents (electrons) from cytosolic NADH into the mitochondrial matrix (reducing oxaloacetate to malate, which enters mitochondria and re-forms NADH), yielding 2.5 ATP via Complex I of the respiratory chain.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 43 (PDF p. 45)

explanations.explanation_text: Oxaloacetate in the cytosol is reduced to malate to pick up electrons; the primary aim is electron transport into mitochondria, not cytosolic oxaloacetate production for glycolysis.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 43 (PDF p. 45)

explanations.explanation_text: Citrate export to the cytosol for de novo fatty acid synthesis is mediated by the tricarboxylate transporter and cleaved by ATP-citrate lyase, not the malate shuttle.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 44, 76 (PDF pp. 46, 78)

explanations.explanation_text: Acetyl-CoA is transported out of the mitochondria into the cytosol as citrate, not via the malate shuttle.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 44, 76 (PDF pp. 46, 78)

explanations.explanation_text: Galactokinase (GALK) catalyzes the initial phosphorylation of galactose to galactose 1-phosphate using ATP.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 66 (PDF p. 68)

explanations.explanation_text: Galactose 1-phosphate uridyl transferase (GALT) catalyzes the exchange between galactose 1-phosphate and UDP-glucose to yield UDP-galactose and glucose 1-phosphate.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 66 (PDF p. 68)

explanations.explanation_text: Aldose reductase reduces free sugars (glucose, galactose) to polyols (sorbitol, galactitol), consuming NADPH.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 66 (PDF p. 68)

explanations.explanation_text: UDP-galactose 4-epimerase (GALE) catalyzes the freely reversible inversion of configuration at carbon-4, converting UDP-glucose to UDP-galactose (which allows endogenous synthesis of galactose-containing glycolipids and glycoproteins even on a galactose-free diet).
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 66 (PDF p. 68)

explanations.explanation_text: Body temperature changes significantly affect RQ; fever increases ventilation and respiratory washout of CO2, altering the measured quotient.

explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 70 (PDF p. 72)

explanations.explanation_text: In aldolase B deficiency, accumulated fructose-1-phosphate sequesters and traps intracellular inorganic phosphate (Pi), causing severe depletion of hepatic ATP.

explanations.explanation_text: Genetic deficiency of fructokinase causes essential fructosuria without phosphate trapping, hypoglycemia, or hepatic damage.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 65 (PDF p. 67)

explanations.explanation_text: Counter-regulatory hormones are appropriately stimulated in response to hypoglycemia, but their action is ineffective because hepatic gluconeogenic and glycogenolytic enzymes are biochemically blocked.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 66 (PDF p. 68)

explanations.explanation_text: Scurvy is caused by Vitamin C deficiency resulting from inadequate intake of fresh citrus fruits and green vegetables.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 15 (PDF p. 17)

explanations.explanation_text: Because the body relies on endogenous synthesis of nicotinic acid from dietary tryptophan (60 mg tryptophan yields 1 mg niacin), populations relying heavily on unfortified maize develop pellagra (dermatitis, diarrhea, dementia).
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 18, 26 (PDF pp. 20, 28)

explanations.explanation_text: Beriberi is caused by thiamine (Vitamin B1) deficiency, typically seen with diets based on polished white rice.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 17 (PDF p. 19)

explanations.explanation_text: Rickets is caused by deficiency of Vitamin D or calcium in growing children, leading to defective bone mineralization.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed pp. 10, 24, 29 (PDF pp. 12, 26, 31)

explanations.explanation_text: Because aerobic oxidative phosphorylation is defective, cells rely on anaerobic glycolysis, causing increased (rather than decreased) lactic acid production and lactic acidosis.

explanations.explanation_text: Tissues with high metabolic energy demands (such as skeletal muscle, CNS, and cardiac muscle) are severely affected by defective oxidative phosphorylation, leading to progressive muscle weakness, exercise intolerance, and skeletal muscle atrophy.

explanations.explanation_text: Central nervous system function is impaired (encephalopathy, ataxia, seizures), not enhanced, due to neuronal ATP starvation.

explanations.explanation_text: Proteins have a physical heat value of 5.3 Cal/g in a bomb calorimeter (oxidizing nitrogen fully to nitric acid), but physiologically in the body, complete oxidation of nitrogen would cause severe acidosis; thus, nitrogen is converted into urea and excreted in urine, carrying away unoxidized chemical energy and yielding a physiological value of only 4.1 Cal/g.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 5

explanations.explanation_text: The difference is not due to incomplete gastrointestinal digestion, but rather to the incomplete metabolic oxidation of amino acid nitrogen in tissue metabolism.
explanations.source_document: Physio - القسم.pdf, p. 5

explanations.explanation_text: Carbohydrates and fats undergo complete oxidation in vivo, matching their physical values; proteins do not undergo complete oxidation.

explanations.explanation_text: Myeloperoxidase utilizes hydrogen peroxide and chloride ions to synthesize hypochlorous acid (HOCl) inside phagolysosomes.

explanations.explanation_text: Catalase is an antioxidant protective enzyme that decomposes hydrogen peroxide into water and molecular oxygen (2 H2O2 -> 2 H2O + O2).
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 99 (PDF p. 101)

explanations.explanation_text: Superoxide dismutase (SOD) detoxifies and converts superoxide into hydrogen peroxide (2 O2•- + 2 H+ -> H2O2 + O2), rather than generating superoxide.
explanations.source_document: Bio - القسم.pdf, printed p. 59 (PDF p. 61)

explanations.explanation_text: NADPH oxidase, located in the plasma membrane of phagocytic leukocytes, catalyzes the one-electron reduction of molecular oxygen using NADPH (O2 + NADPH -> O2•- + NADP+ + H+), generating superoxide anion during the respiratory burst to destroy phagocytosed bacteria.

explanations.explanation_text: Medium-chain fatty acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (MCAD) deficiency is the most common inborn error of lipid catabolism, directly impairing the beta-oxidation of medium-chain fatty acids (C6 to C12) in mitochondria, leading to profound fasting hypoglycemia, hypoketonemia, lethargy, and dicarboxylic aciduria.

explanations.explanation_text: The hexose monophosphate pathway generates NADPH and ribose 5-phosphate and is not directly impaired by MCAD mutations.
